ADNOC & Partner News.title: Adnoc to give away 100 tickets for Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix; how to apply
ADNOC & Partner News.summary: Adnoc to give away 100 tickets for Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix; how to apply Khaleej Times
bullets: ADNOC, a partner of the Formula 1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, is giving away 100 free tickets for the season's race weekend. Fifty winners will each receive two tickets, one for themselves and one for a guest. Of these, 15 winners get two Grandstand Passes each, 20 get two After-Race Concert Tickets each and 15 get two Abu Dhabi Experience Tickets each.

Entrants must complete a form at www.adnoc.ae/adgp with their name, Instagram username and phone number before entries close on 1 December 2026. Winners will be drawn at random on 2 December and contacted by email or SMS. They must respond within 48 hours or the prize may go to a reserve winner. E-tickets will be sent by 3 December. They are non-transferable and non-refundable, and winners cover their own travel, food and other expenses.

ADNOC & Partner News.title: UAE Team Emirates-XRG development rider sent on rare loan transfer move
ADNOC & Partner News.summary: UAE Team Emirates-XRG development rider sent on rare loan transfer move Cyclingnews
bullets: Marcos Freire, the 20-year-old son of three-time world champion Oscar Freire, has been sent on loan from UAE Team Emirates Gen Z to Spanish amateur team Caja Rural-Alea for most of the 2027 season. He signed for the development team in 2025 and raced two seasons with it. He will ride the Spanish domestic circuit from January to August, with a possible spell as a stagiaire at UAE Team Emirates-XRG to follow if he impresses.

The move was brokered by UAE Team Emirates-XRG Sport Director Matxin Joxean Fernandez. Freire will keep his nutritionist, coach and other resources from the UAE team while wearing different colours. Caja Rural-Alea is a feeder squad to ProTeam Caja Rural-Seguros RGA, and its graduates include Abel Balderstone, who joins UAE Team Emirates-XRG next season. Freire said the team will hold a training camp in Mojácar, Almería, on 14 December.
ADNOC & Partner News.copy:
In a move more akin to the world of football than professional cycling, Marcos Freire, the son of three-time world champion Oscar Freire, has been sent ‘on loan’ to a Spanish amateur team for most of the 2027 season.

Freire signed for UAE Team Emirates Gen Z in 2025, racing two seasons with the development team. From January, the 20-year-old will ride for Caja Rural-Alea, a Spanish club team and feeder squad to ProTeam Caja Rural-Seguros RGA, which competed in the 2026 men’s Tour de France.
ADNOC & Partner News.label: CYCLING
ADNOC & Partner News.line: [UAE Team Emirates Gen Z rider Marcos Freire is loaned to Caja Rural-Alea] for the 2027 season, a rare move in cycling.
ADNOC & Partner News.angle: Shows how UAE Team Emirates-XRG manages its development pathway, with Freire's loan and possible stagiaire spell feeding its talent pipeline.

bullets: Shabab Al Ahli beat Ajman 3-1 at Rashid Stadium in the ninth round of the ADNOC Pro League, moving up to fourth place with 16 points. Yuri César scored in the 15th minute and Bala doubled the lead in the 27th.

Lithierry Silva pulled a goal back for Ajman in the 72nd minute, before Janouah Guevara Markelo added Shabab Al Ahli's third in the seventh minute of stoppage time. Lithierry Silva pulled a goal back for Ajman in the 72nd minute before Janouah Guevara Markelo added Shabab Al Ahli’s third in the seventh minute of stoppage time.

Greenworks Australia’s partnership with Erebus Motorsport began at the Taupō round of the New Zealand double-header in April 2026, when the brand’s branding first appeared on the front guard of Jobe Stewart’s Chevrolet Camaro. Competitor News.title: Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion
Competitor News.summary: Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion The Guardian
Competitor News.copy:
The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action.

Fifa is a signatory to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”. They can have their status as a signatory removed, however, if “sincerity in participation or ability to participate is a cause for concern”.

The French team, ranked second in the Women's WorldTour at the end of 2026, has signed a five-year deal with oil and gas giant TotalEnergies, one of France's biggest companies.

bullets: FDJ United-Suez will become TotalEnergies-FDJ United in 2027 after the French energy company signed a five-year title sponsorship deal, its first involvement in women's cycling. TotalEnergies replaces Suez as naming sponsor, while FDJ United, title sponsor since 2017, stays on as second naming partner. The deal was announced on Monday.

The deal follows TotalEnergies ending its title sponsorship of Jean-René Bernaudeau's men's team, which it has backed since 2016, at the close of this year. Team manager Stephen Delcourt said talks began after the Tour de France, helped by TotalEnergies' existing partnerships with ASO for the Tour de France and Paris-Roubaix Femmes. He called it the longest deal in the team's history and an important signal for women's cycling. TotalEnergies also appears on the Netcompany Ineos jersey, and its future there is unclear.

Wider Sports News.summary: LFP secures key court ruling to deploy real-time piracy blocking Sportcal
bullets: The LFP has won a Paris Judicial Court ruling, issued on 20 November, allowing it to block pirate streams automatically and in real time during Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 matches. It is the first ruling to authorise the mechanism created by France's law of 3 August 2026. An automated system is expected to be operational in the coming weeks under the supervision of regulator Arcom, replacing weekly updates and manual approval.

The LFP said the system would shorten the time between identifying and blocking a pirate service, protecting the value of audiovisual rights and club revenues. It comes as the league runs a tender, open from 3 November to 3 December, for five seasons from 2027-28 to 2031-32, with a single Ligue 1 package and exclusive distribution of Ligue 1+. Ligue 1's domestic rights have fallen significantly in value over seven years.

Wider Sports News.title: Argentina bans online betting by minors, gambling sponsorships
Wider Sports News.summary: Argentina bans online betting by minors, gambling sponsorships Buenos Aires Times
bullets: Argentina's Senate has unanimously passed, by 72 votes, legislation banning minors from online gambling and prohibiting betting companies from advertising, promoting or sponsoring gambling, including on sports kits. The ban covers the internet, social media, audiovisual media and outdoor advertising, with advertising allowed only inside casinos, bingo halls, racecourses, betting venues and lottery agencies. Unauthorised operators face prison sentences of three to eight years.

The law will force Argentine football to rewrite commercial deals. Boca Juniors and River Plate hold the two biggest betting sponsorships, both running until 2028 and now to be renegotiated, and the AFA and top flight must also adapt. Footballers, coaches, referees and influencers can no longer feature in betting campaigns, and broadcasters must remove betting adverts during matches.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Argentina's Senate has unanimously passed legislation banning minors from online gambling and prohibiting betting companies from advertising, promoting or sponsoring gambling on sports kits, a move aimed at tackling gambling addiction among young people.

The bill passed with 72 votes in favour, both in the general vote and on individual articles, following an agreement between the ruling La Libertad Avanza (LLA) party and the Peronist opposition.

bullets: Rabobank will become title sponsor of the Visma | Lease a Bike women's team from 2027, when the squad will race as the Rabobank | Lease a Bike Women's Pro Cycling Team. The deal is the next step in a partnership that began in July 2025, when the Dutch bank returned to cycling as a partner of the men's, women's and development teams. Visma moves from title sponsor to founding partner of the organisation.

The team said the deal reflects Rabobank's confidence in the squad and its ambition to grow women's cycling, with joint initiatives planned to encourage more girls to cycle. CEO Richard Plugge called it a special moment, while Rabobank's Carlo van Kemenade tied the move to its identity as a cooperative bank. Elsewhere, Demi Vollering's French team will be renamed TotalEnergies-FDJ United in 2027, with Red Bull already on board as a major sponsor.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Rabobank is, of course, a well-known name in cycling, although its departure in 2012—due to the troubling doping scandals in the cycling peloton—wasn’t exactly on good terms. After it also parted ways with the women’s team in 2016, the Dutch bank was absent from the cycling scene for several years. That is, until 2025, when it suddenly began sponsoring teams again.

In July of that year, it returned to Visma | Lease a Bike, initially as a partner of the men’s, women’s, and development teams. It is also affiliated with the Dutch cycling federation and TeamNL, and organises events such as the Rabo NXT Classic, Ready2Race, and the Rabobank Dikke Banden Races.

Wider Sports News.title: Bodø/Glimt lead global football clubs with 555 per cent social media growth in 2026
Wider Sports News.summary: Football Benchmark data covering January to November highlights Norwegian club's growing international reach. The post Bodø/Glimt lead global football clubs with 555 per cent social media growth in 2026 appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.copy:
Bodø/Glimt recorded the highest percentage increase in social media followers among the world’s leading football clubs in 2026, with their combined Instagram and TikTok audience increasing by 555 per cent between 1st January and 17th November, according to data platform Football Benchmark.

The club’s following grew from approximately 136,000 to 888,000, placing them at the top of Football Benchmark’s ranking of the ten fastest-growing clubs by percentage. Their 555 per cent growth rate was more than 2.7 times that of Chicago Fire FC, the second-ranked club, which recorded an increase of 205 per cent, with Turkish side Trabzonspor registering 140 per cent growth closing in the first three clubs with the biggest digital increase. Also worth highlighting is the contrast with Como 1907, the emerging force in Italian football, which ranked fourth with 138 per cent growth – more than five times lower than Bodø/Glimt’s figure. The analysis took into account only clubs with at least 100k total followers across Instagram and TikTok.

Wider Sports News.title: MLB launches preventative suit against MLBPA as lockout looms
Wider Sports News.summary: MLB launches preventative suit against MLBPA as lockout looms Sportcal
bullets: Major League Baseball has filed a class action lawsuit against the MLB Players Association, saying it has "a reasonable and imminent fear" that the union will use antitrust litigation as a tactic. Collective bargaining talks have shown little progress, making a lockout in 2027 likely. MLB wants the courts to establish that a lockout is legal under its antitrust exemption, or otherwise not an unreasonable restraint on trade.

MLB says the union could decertify itself, a move the league calls a "sham", so that players could sue under the Curt Flood Act and claim a lockout is illegal. The dispute centres on MLB's push for a salary cap, which the union opposes. The MLBPA called the suit "frivolous" and said MLB should bargain in good faith. The Milwaukee Brewers, a small-payroll team, won the World Series 4-1.
Wider Sports News.copy:

bullets: Foot Locker has been named presenting partner of the NBA Manchester Game, in which the New Orleans Pelicans will face the San Antonio Spurs at Co-op Live. It will be the first NBA regular-season game in Manchester. Foot Locker will deliver fan engagement activity in the build-up, across NBA programming in the city and inside the arena on game night.

The agreement builds on the retailer's existing role as an NBA marketing partner in Europe. The fixture is the NBA's second game in Manchester and the 20th involving an NBA team in England since 1993, as part of the league's efforts to grow its audience and commercial presence in the UK. The Spurs roster includes Victor Wembanyama, while the Pelicans feature Zion Williamson. The partnership links basketball with sneaker culture, with retail, fashion and fan experiences planned around the event.

bullets: CONCACAF has renewed and expanded its partnership with Mexican betting company Caliente.mx, which stays an official sponsor in Mexico. bullets: The Confederation of African Football has signed the Tanzania Tourism Board as an official sponsor of the 2027 men's Africa Cup of Nations, which will be held across Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda between 19 June and 17 July. The partnership will use the global appeal of African football to attract visitors and investment to Tanzania, which has never hosted the tournament before.

CAF's Samson Adamu called the deal a milestone that will raise Tanzania's global visibility, while TTB director general Thereza Mugobi said it aims to turn the opportunity into more visitor arrivals and business. CAF also announced a two-edition deal with Coca-Cola this week covering 2027 and 2028, and is seeking hosts for the 2028, 2031 and 2033 editions, with a deadline of 8 December. It reported a 2025-26 profit of $31.2 million on revenue of $284 million.

bullets: The NBA is creating a €10 billion (US$10.9 billion) infrastructure fund to back arenas and entertainment districts across Europe, supporting its planned European league due to launch in 2027. Backers include Apollo Sports Capital, Ares Management, KKR's Arctos, Blackstone, HPS Investment Partners, JP Morgan, Sixth Street and Stonepeak.

The fund will pay for renovating existing arenas to NBA standards and building venues in cities without one, helping the most attractive franchises reach US$1 billion valuations. London, Manchester, Paris, Lyon, Madrid and Barcelona are among the cited target cities, and one study suggests more than €24 billion in gross value and nearly 15,000 jobs. Fiba backs NBA Europe but Euroleague does not, and Euroleague is pursuing its own move to a franchise structure.

Wider Sports News.title: New documents reveal SEC’s role in preventing mandatory media-rights pooling in PCSA
Wider Sports News.summary: New documents reveal SEC’s role in preventing mandatory media-rights pooling in PCSA Awful Announcing
bullets: Emails obtained through public records requests show that keeping its ESPN media deal and staying out of the proposed media pool was a main SEC objective in the Protect College Sports Act. The SEC told senators it would not support the bill unless media-rights pooling was optional, and Commissioner Greg Sankey told members to decline invitations from Saving College Sports, the bill's main advocacy backer, over its support for centralised media-rights negotiations.

Senate Commerce Committee staff later offered changes, including voluntary participation, protection from lawsuits over staying out of the pool and scheduling exemptions for non-participants. Sankey told presidents on 31 July the committee had moved substantially in the SEC's direction. Further revisions protected existing television agreements, including ESPN's SEC deal, from being overridden by a pool.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Awful Announcing previously documented how ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro was lobbying New York Yankees President Randy Levine, a leader of the president’s college sports committee and advocate for the Protect College Sports Act, to protect the network’s television deal with the SEC. New documents show the goal was mutual from the SEC’s side.

Emails obtained via public records requests detail how one of the conference’s main objectives with the bill was keeping its lucrative media deal with ESPN and staying out of the PCSA’s proposed media pool. They show the SEC telling senators it wouldn’t support the PCSA unless media rights pooling was optional and telling its members to turn down meetings with the bill’s primary advocacy backer, Saving College Sports, because of the group’s support for the provision.
Wider Sports News.label: SPORTS BUSINESS
Wider Sports News.line: [SEC emails reveal push] to keep media-rights pooling optional and protect its ESPN deal in the Protect College Sports Act.
Wider Sports News.angle: The story shows how rights holders defend existing media deals in legislation. It has limited direct relevance to ADNOC's properties.

Wider Sports News.title: From Naming Rights to Brand Ownership: ENGIE Open 2026 Connecting Tennis, Local Culture, and Immersion in the Sport
Wider Sports News.summary: From Naming Rights to Brand Ownership: ENGIE Open 2026 Connecting Tennis, Local Culture, and Immersion in the Sport Roastbrief US
Wider Sports News.copy:
Florianópolis, November 2026 – Recognized for its ongoing investment in the development of tennis in Brazil, ENGIE Brasil reinforces the role of sport as a strategic pillar for relationship-building and brand development. At the ENGIE Open 2026—taking place from November 22 to 29 at the Lagoa Iate Clube (LIC)—the company, in collaboration with the agency Paim, is bringing a comprehensive experience to the courts of the Santa Catarina capital. This approach marks an evolution in the brand’s presence at the event, integrating a unique visual identity—inspired by local traditions—with an experiential framework designed to engage everyone from the general public to business and institutional leaders.

The strategy developed for this edition is built upon an experiential framework featuring three levels of engagement, tailored to different audience profiles: the “Open” level (aimed at the general public and fans, offering free arena access, high-performance matches, a social hub, and the official event store); the “Experience” level (featuring active, scheduled activities such as sports clinics, on-court challenges, and exclusive interactions with athletes); and the “Exclusive” level (a platform for hospitality and strategic networking).

Wider Sports News.title: Kraft Heinz isn’t afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship
Wider Sports News.summary: Kraft Heinz isn’t afraid to get cheesy with its NFL sponsorship Marketing Brew
Wider Sports News.copy:
The NFL has gotten a little bit cheesier this season—and fans can’t just blame the league’s scriptwriters. Earlier this year, Kraft Heinz inked a five-year, global partnership with the league for brands in its portfolio including Kraft, Velveeta, Philadelphia, and Kraft Mac & Cheese. It’s the first time multiple Kraft Heinz brands have been involved in the same long-term partnership, according to Ryan Djabbarah, the company’s head of sports and entertainment marketing—and halfway through the season, his team is already seeing results.

Their strategy, Djabbarah told Marketing Brew, has been based largely on weaving Kraft Heinz brands into NFL fan experiences in ways that are whimsical and funny while also adding value—like their latest activation, which reimagines end-zone pylons as blocks of cheese for Thanksgiving weekend as part of a Velveeta product giveaway.

bullets: The US House of Representatives will soon consider a slightly changed version of the Protect College Sports Act, which has already passed the Senate and must be signed by the end of the year to become law. The House version would let conferences expand to as many as 22 teams, two more than the Senate version allows. It would also bar schools with $50 million or more in media-rights revenue from using student fees to subsidise sport.

The bill passed the Senate 77-22 last month. It locks in rules on how athletes are paid and adds protections for Olympic sports. It also includes an antitrust exemption that would block many lawsuits, including those over eligibility. Democrats in the House have raised concerns about athletes' rights. The NCAA has urged member schools to lobby representatives, saying consideration could begin on 30 November. President Donald Trump has repeated his support, saying colleges would otherwise go bankrupt.

Wider Sports News.copy:
The timeline is accelerating for the NFL’s expedited media rights negotiations. John Ourand of Puck reported Thursday that the NFL is now believed to want its new media rights deals completed before the new season begins in September, earlier than the fall timeframe that had been previously reported. The league is expected to negotiate and announce its new deals one-by-one, starting with Paramount and then Fox, Ourand wrote, with all of them taking effect immediately.

Technically, the NFL does not have the ability to exit its current media rights deals until after the 2029 season at the earliest (2030 for ESPN), but there is little expectation that any of the league’s partners will oppose the expedited talks. According to Ourand, it is believed that the new contracts will run through the 2033 or 2034 seasons, meaning that the existing rightsholders can lock up NFL rights for the next seven or eight years by agreeing to the early talks. Currently, the networks are guaranteed only four additional seasons if they choose to wait for the league’s contractual opt-out.

Wider Sports News.summary: MLB’s Local Media Rights Emerge As Focus in Labor Fight Front Office Sports
Wider Sports News.copy:
The future of MLB’s local media business has become a central element in the sport’s labor battle, providing yet another substantial layer to the already fractious situation. For the last six months, MLB club owners have proposed to pool the local media revenue of all 30 clubs as part of a sought-after economic system that would implement a hard salary cap and floor. Most recently, management has updated its cap offer to the MLB Players Association to a 2028 implementation, and vows there will be “no compromise” on the pursuit of a cap as the Dec. 1 expiration of the current labor deal and an expected lockout thereafter approach.

The pooling of local media revenues, and a promise to end regional blackouts that have long frustrated fans, were also part of a video recently distributed by MLB to fans. Throughout the entrenched negotiations, though, two key questions have persisted: Why are the local media and salary cap issues so deeply linked, and why couldn’t owners just agree on their own to pool that revenue, similar to how the NFL operates?

Wider Sports News.summary: The billion-dollar boat race: How SailGP is changing the business of sport The National
bullets: SailGP, the franchise-based sailing league co-founded by Sir Russell Coutts and Larry Ellison, generates revenue through team sales, host-city fees, global sponsorships and media rights. Managing director Andrew Thompson said team budgets are capped at $10 million per season and boats are identical. Races are held in 13 locations across five continents, and the league has risen from four boats to 13, with a 14th joining next season.

Thompson said demand for host venues has surged, with a race weekend estimated to bring $20 million to a local economy. Hong Kong and Rome have been announced for 2027, and premium partners include Rolex and Emirates. Teams now trade at more than $75 million, with Amway chairman Doug Devos paying $60 million for the Danish boat. Teams are capped at 20, and boats 15 and 16 join in 2028.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Andrew Thompson remembers clearly how it all began. Soon after the 2017 America’s Cup, Sir Russell Coutts, the New Zealand-born sailing legend, and the Oracle technology billionaire Larry Ellison were contemplating how to make the sport more appealing to fans and commercially viable.

They had a broad outline in mind, one that married Coutts’ sailing expertise with Ellison’s brilliant mind, but they couldn’t quite nail down the format. Coutts turned to Thompson, a former Deloitte accountant with a lifelong passion for sport, who worked on the 2012 London Olympics, widely regarded as one of the most successful ever. At the time, Thompson was chief financial officer of the America’s Cup.

One buyer named Netflix as the frontrunner, and Fifa is selling English and Spanish rights together for the first time.

Fox paid $485m for English-language rights to the 2026 World Cup and NBC Universal's Telemundo paid $600m for Spanish-language rights. Wider Sports News.title: High Match Tempo Linked to Greater Sponsorship Visibility in Broadcast Study
Wider Sports News.summary: High Match Tempo Linked to Greater Sponsorship Visibility in Broadcast Study Bioengineer.org
Wider Sports News.copy:
A comparative computer vision analysis of European cup soccer broadcasts found that sponsorship visibility reached significantly higher levels during matches characterized by high in-game action and tempo. In an observational investigation published in BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation, researchers recorded a peak sponsorship visibility performance index score of 1,446 points during a high-action intensity match, whereas the maximum efficiency score recorded during a lower-tempo, highly controlled fixture was 23.93 percent lower. The findings demonstrate that brand visibility in digital sports broadcasting is strongly tied to immediate match dynamics rather than overall broadcast length alone.

The team sought to investigate the relational associations connecting dynamic game content to sponsorship efficiency within digital broadcasting environments. Using an exploratory, comparative framework across two distinct European cup fixtures, the authors evaluated how shifting phases of live gameplay and production choices influence commercial exposure on digital streaming platforms.

Wider Sports News.title: Revolut under judicial administration: what is at stake for its Audi F1 sponsorship
Wider Sports News.summary: Revolut under judicial administration: what is at stake for its Audi F1 sponsorship RTR Sports Marketing
bullets: On 16 November 2026 the Court of Milan placed the Italian branch of Revolut Bank, the bank that gives its name to the Audi Revolut F1 Team, under judicial administration for one year. The Milan public prosecutor's office requested the order over alleged serious shortcomings in anti-money-laundering controls, and the Guardia di Finanza carried it out. Prosecutors allege that people under investigation or already convicted used the accounts, with tens of millions of euros passing through them.

The RTR Sports Marketing analysis argues that Audi is unlikely to change the contract in the short term. The bank remains open and the order is not a conviction, so the real risk lies in communications. Revolut says it will cooperate fully and that its Italian services continue normally. The piece cites F1 precedent: Mercedes suspended its FTX deal on 11 November 2022, the day FTX filed for bankruptcy protection.
Wider Sports News.copy:
In my view, in the short term, almost nothing. On 16 November 2026 a Milan court placed the Italian branch of Revolut, the bank that gives its name to the Audi Revolut F1 Team, under judicial administration for one year. The court granted the request of the Milan public prosecutor’s office, which alleges serious shortcomings in the bank’s anti-money-laundering controls. The bank stays open, though, and the order is not a conviction: that is why I believe Audi will leave the contract alone. The real risk lies in communications, because for a bank the product is trust.

Suppose you are the head of communications at a Formula 1 team. One morning the name written on your car is in the headlines for a reason that has nothing to do with overtaking. What do you do? Do you take the logo off before the next race? Do you ring the sponsor to find out what it is going to say? Do you put out a statement? Or do you wait, hoping the story slides down the page?

Wider Sports News.summary: Four-year agreement makes US sportswear giant first brand to supply match ball for all three Uefa men’s club competitions. The post Nike ends Adidas’ Champions League ball reign with €40m-a-year deal appeared first on SportsPro .
bullets: Nike will become the official match ball provider of the Uefa Champions League from next season, ending Adidas' 25-year association with the competition. The deal runs until the end of the 2030/31 campaign and also sees Nike replace Kipsta as ball supplier for the Europa League and Conference League, the first time one company has supplied all three Uefa men's club competitions.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but SportsPro understands the deal is worth around €40 million (US$44 million) a year, which the Financial Times said doubled the value of the current agreement. Uefa club competition rights owner UC3 and its sales agency Relevent Football Partners entered exclusive talks with Nike in April after a tender process. Adidas remains ball supplier for the women's tournament and Uefa national team competitions, including Euro 2028 and the Nations League.

Wider Sports News.title: Canadian insurance sponsorships are reshaping carrier brand strategy
Wider Sports News.summary: Canadian insurance sponsorships are reshaping carrier brand strategy Insurance Business
Wider Sports News.copy:
Canadian insurance sponsorships reached a new level of strategic intent in 2026, and the stakes for brokers are more concrete than they might appear. Carriers that do not distribute through independent brokers are using sports and community partnerships as their primary mechanism for building consumer familiarity – the kind of name recognition that broker relationships provide for other carriers organically. The broker question is not abstract: IBC’s own survey data shows the share of Canadian insurance clients who say they always rely fully on their broker’s recommendation to choose an insurer has fallen from 45% in 2024 to 35% in 2026. When clients arrive at a broker conversation having already formed a view of a carrier, that is partly a function of brand exposure. Sports sponsorship is one of the main ways carriers are creating that exposure.

The numbers frame the gap. According to the Canadian Life and Health Insurance Association’s (CLHIA) 2026 annual factbook, released October 20, 2026, 84% of life insurance in Canada – totalling $6.2 trillion in coverage across 23 million Canadians – is purchased through individual agents and advisors. Carriers that cannot access that channel must build consumer recognition another way. They are spending more doing so: according to the 2026 Canadian Sponsorship Landscape Study, released August 18, 2026, by T1 and the Sponsorship Marketing Council Canada, total sponsorship spending in Canada reached $4.7 billion – with brands planning to increase investment further.

Wider Sports News.title: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship
Wider Sports News.summary: Sid Lee Sport partners with Guinness to measure the true commercial value of sports sponsorship European Sponsorship Association
bullets: Sid Lee Sport, working with sister agency Kepler, is evaluating Guinness's global sports sponsorship portfolio to assess the commercial impact of its football and rugby partnerships. The project covers six markets (Great Britain, Ireland, Kenya, the United States, Indonesia and South Korea) and nine rights holders. These include the Premier League, Arsenal, Aston Villa, Newcastle United and the Guinness Men's and Women's Six Nations.

The evaluation uses KIP, a proprietary platform, to analyse three years of sales, brand and partnership data and isolate the incremental commercial impact of the investments. It looks beyond exposure at broadcast media value, digital reach, stadium pouring rights, fan research and experiential activation. Sid Lee Sport's Mike Grumbridge said the industry relies heavily on traditional metrics such as media exposure and reach. The findings are intended to inform future investment decisions.
Wider Sports News.copy:
Major evaluation project spans six markets and nine rights holders, moving beyond traditional media valuation to assess the business impact of Guinness’s global sponsorship portfolio.

Global sports marketing agency Sid Lee Sport, working alongside sister agency, Kepler, is undertaking a major evaluation of Guinness’s global sports sponsorship portfolio, designed to establish a clearer understanding of the commercial impact of its football and rugby partnerships.

It reviewed ongoing efforts to apply best practices in sustainability, innovation and governance.

bullets: The 2026-27 season is the first in which Premier League clubs cannot carry gambling sponsors on the front of their shirts. Bally's and Betano were replaced by technology, tourism and financial services firms, while Stake moved to shirt sleeves. A University of Bristol analysis found the ban removed about 10% of gambling messages on the opening weekend. Roughly half of that was offset by more exposure on sleeves, training kits and LED pitch-side screens.

Half the league needed new front-of-shirt sponsors: Bournemouth moved Vitality from stadium to shirt, Brentford added Indeed and Nottingham Forest signed Marex. Chelsea signed crypto firm Circle after starting the season with a blank shirt. Ampere Analytics estimates that the eight clubs needing new sponsors saw combined annual deal value rise from £67 million to £75 million. Clubs in the three divisions below remain free to sign gambling deals, and Betano will sponsor Euro 2028.

Pirelli took over from Bridgestone as F1's sole tyre supplier in 2011 and for much of its first decade it faced little in the way of concerted challenge when renewal time rolled around. That has changed in recent years. Having walked away from F1 in 2010, citing costs and a "strategic realignment" following the global financial crisis, Bridgestone threw its hat in the ring during the most recent tender process in 2023, and is known to be preparing a pitch for the next one.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Formula 1 races will become shorter in 2027, with the standard distance falling from 305km to 290km. That means most Grands Prix will lose two or three laps, depending on the circuit.

The change is tied to planned fuel-flow adjustments in the 2027 power-unit rules. F1 will allow more fuel to flow through the engines, which means cars need more fuel to finish a race. Teams designed their 2026 fuel tanks around the current rules and want to avoid building new chassis.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: FIA details F1 engine freeze and imposes testing restrictions ahead of V8 return Autosport
bullets: The FIA has confirmed that development of current F1 hybrid V6 power units will be frozen from the 13th race of the 2028 season, after which only reliability updates are allowed. Restrictions also apply to the 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 due in 2030: no single-cylinder dyno work until 1 October 2027 and no full power unit dyno work until 1 July 2028. Newcomers such as General Motors, for Cadillac, are exempt.

FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis told Autosport the aim is to avoid manufacturers running two parallel programmes for cost reasons, and to stop competitive manufacturers switching to 2030 work earlier than those chasing. The freeze is agreed with all parties. The next step is changes to ADUO so that no manufacturer, such as Honda, is left far behind by mid-2028, though no final decision has been made.

Using iPhone cameras for big events is no longer a novelty. Apple has been shooting its event videos and ad spots with iPhone Pro models outfitted with cinema-grade lenses, SSD storage and broadcasting gear for several years now. bullets: Toyota Gazoo Racing's Seth Quintero and Andrew Short finished third overall in the 35th Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge, which was enough to secure the Drivers' and Navigators' titles in the 2026 FIA World Rally-Raid Championship. They moved onto the podium on Friday's final stage and finished five points ahead of Dacia's Nasser Saleh Al-Attiyah and Fabian Lurquin after a five-round season. Quintero, 24, becomes the youngest champion in the series' history.

Al-Attiyah won the event for the third time in a row, with Sébastien Loeb and Edouard Boulanger second, 2min 44sec behind. Emirati Mansour Al-Helai and navigator Khaled Al-Kendi won the SSV category and finished ninth overall. Twenty crews made the start list for what the FIA calls the UAE's premier off-road event. The American Toyota DKR GR Hilux pairing was able to move up to the final podium position on the last stage on Friday and amass enough points to prevent Dacia’s Nasser Saleh Al-Attiyah and Fabian Lurquin from snatching the championship to add to the Qatari’s sixth overall success at the Abu Dhabi Desert Challenge. The gap between the two was just five points at the end of a gruelling five-round season.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Qatar GP organisers keen to show world 'real situation' amid safety concerns ESPN
bullets: Formula 1's Qatar Grand Prix is going ahead as planned this weekend, on 29 November, with organisers hoping it will show a global audience "the real situation" in the country. The race has been under uncertainty all year after US and Israeli bombing of Iran prompted retaliatory strikes on Qatar and other states, and F1 cancelled its April races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

F1 maintains it is safe to finish the season in the Middle East, with the Abu Dhabi finale due on 6 December. It cites government travel advice, valid travel insurance and assurances from local authorities, although the UK Foreign Office warned on 18 November that the situation remains "deeply unpredictable". Qatar Motor and Motorcycle Federation president Abdul Rahman bin Abdullatif Al Mannai said Qatar never considered moving the race and that emergency procedures match previous years. He added that the 8 November MotoGP round at Lusail helped show viewers the real situation.

bullets: The FIA has penalised Williams and Alpine for breaches of the 2025 cost-cap and financial reporting rules. Williams exceeded the cap by £627,000 (0.48%), which the FIA classed as a minor breach arising from an administrative misunderstanding over costs linked to a company restructuring. It faces a financial penalty and a reduction in its aerodynamic testing allowance. Alpine was found guilty of a procedural breach over inaccurate reporting of excluded and adjusted costs and was fined, though it did not overspend.

Audi's protest over the 2026 Italian Grand Prix result has been heard in Paris, with a ruling pending. Audi argues Yuki Tsunoda caused an extra formation lap; if it succeeds, Gabriel Bortoleto would inherit a point and Audi would close on Haas, who lead by three for seventh in the Constructors' Championship. The 21-year-old Brazilian will instead race for Haas in the Qatar Grand Prix and the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix at Yas Marina Circuit, having already stood in at Sao Paulo and Las Vegas.

Freddie Slater, 18, replaces him at Invicta Racing for the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, and is already confirmed as the team's 2027 driver. Alex Dunne is 11 points behind Tsolov. Camara was named Esteban Ocon's replacement at Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season, but with Ocon out at Haas before the Mexico City Grand Prix, Camara was called upon early to take his place alongside Ollie Bearman. After Ryo Hirakawa filled in for the Mexico race, Camara took over in his home race in Sao Paulo and also competed in Las Vegas.

bullets: Standard Chartered and F1 Academy have launched "Drive Further", a multi-year financial skills programme for female racing drivers. It covers sponsorship acquisition, financial planning, budgeting and investment, and combines virtual learning modules, in-person workshops and personalised support. The programme was developed in response to needs identified by the drivers themselves.

Training has already run through 2026, including a session with Steve Brice, Standard Chartered's Global Chief Investment Officer, and an in-person workshop at the United States Grand Prix in Austin. Judy Hsu, CEO of Wealth & Retail Banking at the bank, said the aim is to help young female drivers handle the financial and commercial side of their careers early on. The partners plan to develop the programme with each new cohort of drivers.

The "Drive Further" initiative is a multi-year programme designed to equip female drivers with the practical financial and commercial skills necessary to sustain a career in professional motorsport. Developed in response to needs identified by the drivers themselves, the curriculum focuses on areas where young athletes often face significant pressure, including sponsorship acquisition, financial planning, budgeting, and investment strategies. The programme combines virtual learning modules with in-person workshops and personalised support, leveraging the banking and wealth management expertise of Standard Chartered.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Cadillac Setting Up Fan Zone At F1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Cadillac Setting Up Fan Zone At F1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix GM Authority
bullets: Cadillac will open an exclusive branded Fan Zone at the 2026 Formula 1 Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix at Yas Marina Circuit. It will be open to all attendees from 3 to 6 December, between 10:30 and 20:00. The Cadillac F1 Team will end its debut season at the race, the final round of this year's championship.

The zone will show a replica of the team's MAC-26 race car, displayed for the first time in the region, alongside V-Series road cars and two racing simulators. It also includes an exclusive showroom, VIP terraces and a rooftop terrace with lounge areas and a large LED screen broadcasting the race. The design draws on Cadillac's retail network and corporate identity, with a black-and-white look that mirrors the team's visual style.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Cadillac is preparing to finish its debut season in Formula 1 and has just officially announced that it will have an exclusive branded Fan Zone at the F1 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

General Motors’ luxury brand has announced that it will debut an exclusive Fan Zone during the 2026 Formula 1 Etihad Airways Abu Dhabi Grand Prix – the final race of this year’s premier global motorsport championship, scheduled for early next month. At the event, Cadillac will host its own dedicated stand for fans and the general public throughout the race program, which will run from December 3rd to the 6th at the Yas Marina Circuit.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Cadillac opens a branded Fan Zone] at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, 3–6 December, as its F1 team ends its debut season.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Max Verstappen has suffered a late blow to his preparations for the 2026 Qatar Grand Prix this weekend. The four-time world champion will have to work with a different voice on the team radio after his long-time race engineer, Gianpiero Lambiase, was forced to miss the penultimate round of the season due to personal circumstances.

Red Bull had initially planned for Lambiase to return to Verstappen's side of the garage for the final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However, his unexpected absence from the Lusail International Circuit means performance engineer Tom Hart will take over race engineering duties once again.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Hamilton reveals if he and Leclerc are still free to race after Las Vegas clash
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Hamilton reveals if he and Leclerc are still free to race after Las Vegas clash Yahoo Sports
bullets: Lewis Hamilton has confirmed that he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other in the final two rounds of the season, despite their collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Hamilton spun after contact and finished seventh, while Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for causing the incident and finished tenth, after both failed to reach Q3 on Saturday.

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur asked to meet Leclerc over team radio after the chequered flag and expressed frustration at how events had unfolded. Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 that Ferrari has imposed no new restrictions and that avoiding contact has always been the team's number one rule. He said he and Leclerc had held a good conversation in Qatar, enjoy racing each other and have a good relationship.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Lewis Hamilton has confirmed that he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other in the final two rounds of the season, despite their controversial collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

The two Ferrari drivers were involved in several wheel-to-wheel battles throughout Sunday's race in Las Vegas, with their fight eventually resulting in contact. Hamilton was sent into a spin following the collision with his teammate, while Leclerc subsequently received a 10-second time penalty for causing the incident.

bullets: Three teams have confirmed driver changes for the final two rounds of the 2026 FIA Formula 2 season, at Lusail and Yas Marina. Roman Bilinski joins Hitech, replacing Colton Herta, while Sebastián Montoya moves to DAMS Lucas Oil in place of the British-Polish driver. Nicola Lacorte steps up to the championship with PREMA Racing, taking the seat of the Colombian.

All three drivers have already been confirmed for next season, so the switches give them early experience with their new teams. Bilinski said working with Hitech straight away lets them build a strong foundation for 2027. Montoya said the simulator work helped him learn how DAMS operates, and Lacorte said he would make the most of his last two 2026 races with PREMA to go into next year stronger.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Everything we learned on day one of F1's 2026 Qatar Grand Prix
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Everything we learned on day one of F1's 2026 Qatar Grand Prix The Race
bullets: Formula 1 arrived at Lusail for the Qatar Grand Prix, where Haas confirmed on Thursday that Ollie Bearman will stay with the team in 2027, settling the final open question on the 2027 driver line-up. Asked about his longer-term Ferrari future, Bearman said he hopes to race for Ferrari one day, noting he is in F1 thanks to his 2024 Jeddah debut in place of Carlos Sainz.

Charles Leclerc denied speculation that he holds a contractual number one clause at Ferrari, saying he has no such clause and objecting to questions over his loyalty to the team. George Russell called his failed Las Vegas overtake on Kimi Antonelli his own mistake, after he lost his braking reference, and said his risk level is too high with two races left. Honda said it found no fault on Fernando Alonso's engine, which he parked in Las Vegas with a lap to go.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
The various flavours of Las Vegas fallout took some new twists as Formula 1 arrived at the Qatar Grand Prix, the final 2027 driver line-up question was answered and we had some surprising admissions from George Russell.

Here's everything we learned on day one at Lusail. During the height of internal tension between Haas and Esteban Ocon, team boss Ayao Komatsu bemoaned the modern age of uncorroborated rumours spreading like wildfire around the internet, and in the wake of the latest clash between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in Las Vegas, it seems Ferrari is the latest team to suffer from this phenomenon.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Max Verstappen without Gianpiero Lambiase at Qatar GP as Tom Hart steps in
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Max Verstappen without Gianpiero Lambiase at Qatar GP as Tom Hart steps in Motorsport.com
bullets: Max Verstappen will race at the Qatar Grand Prix at Lusail International Circuit without his regular race engineer, Gianpiero Lambiase, who is absent for personal circumstances. Tom Hart, who has worked for Red Bull since 2013, will step in. Red Bull told Motorsport.com that Lambiase is expected back in Abu Dhabi if his circumstances allow.

Red Bull has rotated the role late in the season so Hart can settle in before Lambiase's expected gardening leave in 2027 and move to McLaren. That makes Hart likely to be Verstappen's permanent race engineer from the start of 2027, though Red Bull has not formally announced it. Early races together brought radio problems in Austin and a feel complaint in Brazil, but communication appeared better in Las Vegas. Verstappen expects Qatar's high-speed corners to be a different challenge.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Max Verstappen will be without his regular right-hand man Gianpiero Lambiase this weekend at the Lusail International Circuit. Red Bull had already opted for a rotation system for the latter part of this Formula 1 season, primarily to allow Tom Hart to settle into the role ahead of his expected permanent appointment while Lambiase is still with the team.

The initial plan was for Lambiase to cover the final two grands prix of the season as Verstappen's race engineer, besides his duties as Red Bull’s head of racing, but he will be absent in Qatar due to personal circumstances. The team told Motorsport.com that Lambiase is expected to return in Abu Dhabi, provided his personal circumstances allow.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Tom Hart replaces Gianpiero Lambiase] as Max Verstappen's race engineer at the Qatar Grand Prix; Lambiase is expected back in Abu Dhabi.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Leclerc furious with integrity being questioned after Hamilton clashes Autosport
bullets: Charles Leclerc said he was angered by questions over his integrity and love for Ferrari after another clash with team-mate Lewis Hamilton, in Las Vegas, where he received a 10-second penalty for causing a spin at Turn 7. The pair have also clashed at Monza, Zandvoort and Mexico. Leclerc finished 10th in Las Vegas, with Hamilton three places higher.

Speaking in Qatar, Leclerc accepted the incident was unacceptable but denied having a clause in his contract, renewed on a multi-year deal in June, that makes him number one driver. He said he and the team are seeking a solution to protect team points. Hamilton's contract runs to the end of 2027. Ferrari are second in the championship with Qatar and Abu Dhabi left.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Photo by: Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images Charles Leclerc was left furious by those ‘questioning his integrity and love for Ferrari’ after yet another clash with Formula 1 team-mate Lewis Hamilton - having urged to find a “solution”.

The Ferrari pair have been at loggerheads several times during the second half of the 2026 F1 campaign, clashing at Monza, Zandvoort and Mexico before their latest spat in Las Vegas.

Speaking to F1 TV after a bruised night in Nevada, Vasseur was asked directly whether Leclerc alone had defied team instructions or if both drivers shared fault in their heated battle for sixth place.

bullets: The FIA found that Williams broke Formula 1's cost cap in the 2025 season, when the limit was $135m (£106m). The team say they unintentionally exceeded it by £627,000, equivalent to a 0.48% overspend, which the FIA placed at the lower end of the minor overspend range of less than 5%.

Williams' accepted breach agreement includes an undisclosed financial penalty and a 1.5% reduction in permitted aerodynamic research and development time for the next 12 months. Alpine also committed a procedural breach without overspending and received an undisclosed financial penalty, and both teams must cover the FIA's investigation costs. The FIA said there was no evidence of bad faith, and Williams said the costs related to changes to its company structure.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Zak Brown rules out McLaren engine programme for F1 2030 Motorsport.com
bullets: Zak Brown has ruled out a McLaren factory engine programme for Formula 1's 2030 engine change, saying the team is "very happy" with its Mercedes partnership. McLaren has been a Mercedes customer since 2021, winning two constructors' titles (2024, 2025), a drivers' championship (2025) and 24 grands prix in that time.

Brown spoke at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, after a season in which engine difficulties had at one point strained relations between the two manufacturers. McLaren is fourth in the standings, 235 points behind champions Mercedes, but has won three times in the second half of 2026. His comments came before Motorsport.com reported F1 plans to limit each manufacturer to two power unit supplies, including its factory team, which could create political tension as McLaren, Alpine and Williams all use Mercedes engines.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Zak Brown has ruled out a factory engine programme for the 2030 Formula 1 campaign as McLaren is “very happy” with its Mercedes partnership. The British marque has been a Mercedes customer since 2021 and has enjoyed vast success in that period, winning two constructors’ titles (2024, 2025), a drivers’ championship (2025) and 24 grands prix.

But F1 is set for its next engine change in 2030 by introducing turbocharged, 2.1-litre V8 power units to replace the current ones that only came in this year, yet have proven to be contentious.

bullets: Standard Chartered and F1 Academy have launched 'Drive Further', a multi-year financial skills initiative to help female drivers handle the financial and commercial decisions of building a motorsport career. It combines virtual learning, in-person workshops and individual support, drawing on the bank's Wealth & Retail Banking expertise.

This season the programme has covered financial planning, budgeting, sponsorship and investment, with input from Standard Chartered's Global Chief Investment Officer, Steve Brice, and an in-person workshop at Round 5 in Austin. The partners will keep developing it in the coming years with each driver cohort. Judy Hsu said early support helps drivers seize opportunities, and F1 Academy's Katie Denver said drivers face sponsorship and financial decisions from a very young age.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Unaired Las Vegas radio reveals Red Bull considered giving up Max Verstappen's lead
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Unaired Las Vegas radio reveals Red Bull considered giving up Max Verstappen's lead Motorsport.com
bullets: Unaired team radio from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix shows Red Bull's pitwall asked Max Verstappen to consider not leading at the Overtake Mode detection point on the penultimate lap. Race engineer Tom Hart said Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was 1.2 seconds behind and Oscar Piastri 1.9. A driver within a second at the Turn 16 detection point gained an extra 0.5 MJ of electrical deployment for the final lap.

Antonelli tried the same tactic in reverse, lifting before Turn 14, which disrupted his car's energy harvesting and left him with no battery. Both McLarens passed him before the final lap. Verstappen won by 0.639 seconds from Lando Norris for his fourth win of 2026 and 75th overall. He is 37 points clear of Lewis Hamilton for second in the drivers' standings, and Red Bull are nine points ahead of McLaren for third in the constructors' before Qatar.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes. In almost any other Formula 1 race, suggesting a race leader deliberately surrender first place with one lap left would sound unthinkable. At the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Red Bull’s pitwall genuinely floated the idea to Max Verstappen.

Team radio messages revealed just how intensely Verstappen and race engineer Tom Hart calculated the closing stages of Saturday night’s 35-lead-change thriller. As early as Lap 39, Verstappen sensed Mercedes had deciphered his deployment pattern down the Strip and pressed his pitwall for a fresh plan.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix comes and goes with expected $800M impact on Southern Nevada - Las Vegas Review-Journal
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix comes and goes with expected $800M impact on Southern Nevada Las Vegas Review-Journal
bullets: The fourth Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix sold out again and is expected to generate around $800 million for Southern Nevada, according to Steve Hill of the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority. The economic impact exceeded $1 billion in the first year, partly because of F1's infrastructure spending, and Hill said it should fall slightly as F1 becomes more efficient. The 2025 race generated $43 million in state and local tax revenue.

The race is contracted through 2037, and Las Vegas Grand Prix CEO Emily Prazer said F1 will improve infrastructure, including a permanent podium, buried utilities, permanent power sources and lighting supports. Set-up now takes 11 weeks and teardown five, compared with nine months of construction before the 2023 race. MGM Resorts' Bill Hornbuckle said the Bellagio Fountain Club sold out for the first time and MGM is committed to hosting it until at least 2034.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
The fourth annual Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix has come and gone as fast as the race cars zoomed down the Strip on Saturday night. The event again sold out, leaving a hefty economic impact on Southern Nevada, tourism and hospitality leaders said.

The three-day mega-event is expected generate around $800 million, according to Steve Hill, president and CEO of the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority. The economic results of the race surpassed $1 billion in its first year, partly tied to what F1 spent on infrastructure for the race, including the 300,000-square-foot pit building on the northeast corner of Harmon Avenue and Koval Lane and paving the entire circuit to race standards. The city can expect the race to continue to see the $800 million weekend, making it the biggest event of any year that a Super Bowl isn’t happening in Las Vegas.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1 BUSINESS
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Las Vegas Grand Prix is expected to generate $800m] for Southern Nevada after a fourth sell-out race, contracted to 2037.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Alba Larsen targets 2027 F1 Academy title after Vegas Formula Live Pulse
bullets: Alba Larsen has set her sights on the 2027 F1 Academy title after ending her season in Las Vegas with a win and a second place. The Ferrari-backed MP Motorsport driver won the reverse-grid race from ninth on the grid, the lowest starting position in series history, and finished 0.320 seconds behind champion Alisha Palmowski in the feature race after a late Safety Car.

The 17-year-old finished fourth in the 2026 standings on 104 points, 80 of them in the final three rounds, and took six podiums in the last seven races, including her first win in Austin. She will return for a third season with Ferrari's backing, while Palmowski moves up to Formula Regional with Rodin Motorsport in 2027.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali Keeps the Las Vegas Grand Prix In-House
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali Keeps the Las Vegas Grand Prix In-House Observer
bullets: Formula 1 said Saturday's Las Vegas Grand Prix sold out. It is the one race the sport promotes itself, and F1 signed a 10-year extension through 2037 in June. F1 counted seven partnership announcements in four days. They included a four-year deal making Whoop its global health and fitness wearable partner and a Nike deal to outfit F1 staff from 2027. Apple streamed all Las Vegas sessions free in the US and will carry every F1 Academy qualifying session and race exclusively in the US next year.

In Las Vegas, F1 keeps the ticket revenue and earns from sponsorship and hospitality, but Liberty Media has not disclosed a profit figure. Saturday tickets averaged $781 on TickPick, down from $889 last year. Steve Hill, CEO of the Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority, estimated this year's economic impact at around $800 million. Former Liberty CEO Greg Maffei told a Sportico conference he thought F1 could be taken private within two years.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Before last year’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali told a roomful of business leaders, “We are here to stay; we are here to grow.” In June, F1 signed a 10-year extension through 2037 for the one race it promotes itself. Saturday’s race sold out, F1 said Monday. To Tiggy Valen, creator of Paddock Project, who attended Thursday’s F1 Business Summit, the message was much the same this time, only more commercial.

“Vegas always feels commercial, but it feels like there’s so much more this year,” Valen tells Observer. “Like every hotel has a car or a merch store, or something else, and it’s kind of everywhere you turn.” At the track, she spotted a Whoop zone, a massive Nike swoosh and new grandstands.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Decision time looms for Colton Herta after 2027 Cadillac F1 snub
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Decision time looms for Colton Herta after 2027 Cadillac F1 snub Motorsport.com
bullets: Cadillac has chosen to keep Valtteri Bottas alongside Sergio Perez for 2027, leaving Colton Herta without a race seat at Formula 1's 11th team. The 26-year-old American, a nine-time IndyCar winner, has reportedly turned down the offered reserve role for now. He has also decided to skip the final two Formula 2 rounds with Hitech, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss said the reserve offer stands and that the seat is open for 2028, with options in other sports also under discussion. The reserve role is understood to be lucrative and could be paired with a one-off Indy 500 outing. IndyCar introduces the all-new Dallara IR-28 in 2028, which makes that year pivotal for Herta's next move.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Cadillac's decision to stick with veteran incumbent Valtteri Bottas to partner Sergio Perez is a choice for continuity and stability after a debut campaign plagued with issues for Formula 1's 11th team in 2026. It also raises key questions over what's next for Colton Herta.

With Cadillac's majority owner TWG enamoured with the prospect of having an American driver in one of its cars before too long, the team spared no expense on bringing Herta over, leaving the comfort of his IndyCar seat with sister team Andretti Global for a now-or-never shot at making it to F1.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: The issue that cost Pierre Gasly a potential "win" at F1's Las Vegas GP
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: The issue that cost Pierre Gasly a potential "win" at F1's Las Vegas GP Motorsport.com
bullets: Pierre Gasly finished fifth in the Las Vegas Grand Prix for Alpine after starting eighth, and said he may have had the pace to win. After 31 of 50 laps he was third behind Max Verstappen and George Russell. He then lost five places in four laps after being told on the radio that the car was overheating and that he had to turn down the power.

Gasly said power was reduced for 45 laps, costing him more than a second a lap in the most extreme mode. He was allowed full power only in the last two laps. He rose to fifth after Russell hit the barriers and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided. It was Alpine's best race of the season, and he remains 10th in the standings. The team will review why the car overheated in conditions as low as 9C.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Pierre Gasly reckons he potentially had the pace to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, had a cooling issue not affected his Alpine Formula 1 car in the closing stages. The Frenchman finished fifth from eighth on the grid, but after 31 of the scheduled 50 laps, Gasly was third behind Red Bull’s eventual winner Max Verstappen and Mercedes’ George Russell.

Yet Gasly suddenly lost five positions within the next four laps, having dropped into eighth behind Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Kimi Antonelli, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Pierre Gasly finished fifth in Las Vegas] after an overheating issue cost him a podium place; he says Alpine had the pace to challenge for the win.

bullets: The Las Vegas Grand Prix has generated $3.2bn in cumulative economic impact for Southern Nevada since its 2023 debut, according to F1. This year's race was the 21st consecutive sell-out and ran over 50 laps with a record number of overtakes. The 2025 race produced $43m in state and local tax revenue, drew 165,000 unique visitors from 49 countries and reached a record worldwide audience of more than 67 million.

The second annual F1 Business Summit was held during the weekend, bringing together leaders from technology, finance, luxury, fashion, hospitality, media, entertainment and sport. Nike and WHOOP signed as new partners and Standard Chartered expanded to become a Global Partner, among seven partnership announcements in four days. F1 says it has 53 million US fans, up 11% from 2023. President and CEO Stefano Domenicali said F1 will return to Las Vegas next year.

bullets: Ritomo Miyata took his first Formula 2 victory in the Madrid Sprint Race, converting a second-place start into a win, and added a third place in the Feature Race after starting ninth. The Hitech driver had qualified inside the top 10 for just the third time this season, and said it was the first time he had stood on a podium, having been promoted to second at Spa last year after penalties to others.

Miyata said he focused on his start because the Madrid layout looked hard to overtake on, then managed the pace and restarts amid Safety Car risk. He said the team had struggled with short-run performance early in the season but had good long-run pace.

Miyata believes his good starting positions were key to his success that weekend, having qualified inside the top 10 for just the third time in the season. “It was an amazing weekend,” reflected Miyata. “At first this year we struggled, especially with short run performance.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Formula 1 driver change creates rare situation seen just once in 77 years Beyond the Flag
bullets: Haas has confirmed that Rafael Camara will drive the final two races of the 2026 season, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. The team dropped Esteban Ocon with five races left and brought in Ryo Hirakawa in Mexico City. Camara, already named Ocon's 2027 replacement, raced in São Paulo and Las Vegas.

Only one seat remains open on the 2027 grid, alongside Camara at Haas, and it would be a major shock if it did not go to Ollie Bearman, who has been with the team since 2025. If so, the season-finale line-up would match the next season's opener, which has happened once in F1's 77-year history, in 2023-24. That followed Daniel Ricciardo replacing Nyck de Vries at AlphaTauri, with Liam Lawson later replacing Ricciardo for the final six races of 2024.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
There has been just one driver change confirmed for the 2027 Formula 1 season thus far, and given the confirmations throughout the rest of the grid, it is unlikely that there will be any more.

That lone change has already been enacted, as Haas dropped Esteban Ocon with five races remaining on the 2026 schedule and brought in Ryo Hirakawa as his replacement in Mexico City.

bullets: TGR Haas F1 Team principal Ayao Komatsu said the team wants partners that offer far more than money and exposure, speaking at the F1 Business Summit in Las Vegas. Haas has agreed new partnerships numbering in double figures during 2026, spanning banking, sportswear, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, sustainability, expenses software and drinks.

Komatsu described Haas as the smallest team on the grid and said it relies on long-term partners who share its values, rather than transactional logo placements. He cited Toyota Gazoo Racing, which became title partner in 2024 after talks with chairman Akio Toyoda, having started as a technology partner. This year's additions include Bradesco, Castore, D.Energy, Dynamo Capital, Emburse, Exein, FIX Network, NeverMile, Singha, TENEX.AI and Toho. He said real return on investment lies in storytelling.

The number of new partnershipss agreed at some point across the 2026 season has reached double-figures as Haas seeks to continue to grow its commercial ecosystem. “I keep saying we are the smallest team, so we cannot do it by ourselves,” Komatsu said at the F1 Business Summit in Las Vegas.

Oracle Red Bull Racing lead McLaren by nine points in the Constructors' Championship, with Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finishing second and third in Las Vegas. Verstappen said his goal is to defend third place for the team. Charles Leclerc and Hamilton collided on lap 38, and George Russell hit the wall on lap 48. The next races are the Qatar Grand Prix on 29 November and the season finale in Abu Dhabi on 6 December.

bullets: Alisha Palmowski clinched the 2026 F1 Academy Drivers' title, and her Campos Racing team won the Teams' Championship alongside Rafaela Ferreira, who finished 11th overall. Both are Red Bull Academy Programme drivers, and both were in their second year in the all-female Formula 4-level series.

The fourth F1 Academy season comprised 14 races across six rounds, starting in Shanghai in March and ending in Las Vegas on 21 November alongside the Formula 1 Grand Prix. Palmowski, 20, secured the title in Austin with around 30 photographers at her car. Ferreira, 21, named Canada, where she led from pole, as her defining moment. Both said the series is tougher than people realise, citing track evolution as a support series to F1 and heavy simulator work.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Alisha Palmowski and Rafaela Ferreira have learned how to stay calm under pressure, helping Campos Racing win the 2026 F1 Teams’ Championship. The Red Bull Academy Programme drivers reflect on their successful second year in the all-female Formula 4–level racing series and tell TODAY.com their improved confidence and execution over the last year secured them the top honors.

“Being at both of our second years, I think we were both able to take a lot of learnings from last year and just execute it a little bit better,” 20-year-old Palmowski, who clinched the 2026 Drivers’ title, says. “I was much more confident going into this year, a lot calmer. Just knew more of what to expect of the whole procedure of F1 Academy. A completely different driver and person than the driver who turned up to Shanghai last year.”

Race CEO Emily Prazer said infrastructure will be improved, including undergrounding utilities and building a permanent podium, while F1 is working with Clark County on permanent fixtures to speed up set-up and tear-down. RACER's Chris Medland described the race as Indy 500-like, with the tow a major factor in the outcome.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
The Las Vegas Grand Prix this past weekend was “a remarkable, breathless offering that saw positions changing multiple times on each lap” -- and was “very Indy 500-esque,” according to Chris Medland of RACER. Not only did the race place “a high demand on power unit deployment, but the tow -- and how to use it -- was a major factor in the outcome.” With a huge pack able to sit in behind the lead car, it “became about avoiding incidents, cleanly navigating the pit stop phase, and then timing your charge to the front.” It was a “unique race where drivers looked capable of climbing through even without a major pace advantage.” On some tracks earlier this F1 season, the layout “almost didn’t matter.” There would be “yo-yoing from the start that would settle down as the race wore on.” But in Las Vegas, there was “no such settling down.” The track layout, “energy challenges and powerful tow all combined with low-speed corners that were less problematic in terms of aerodynamic disruption when closely following another car ahead.” Most viewers of the Indy 500 would “call it an entertaining race regardless of the overriding need to just stay on the lead lap and be near the front for the final stages.” Las Vegas’ characteristics “delivered a challenge along the same lines, and we saw drivers having to think in a similar way to those who have had their eyes on the Borg Warner Trophy” (RACER, 11/22).

CHEF’S KISS: MOTORSPORT’s Filip Cleeren noted the race had 35 lead changes and “felt like the glitzy, battery-assisted street course version of the Indy 500.” It was “quite fitting to see how in America’s artificial entertainment capital, F1 put on an entertaining, if somewhat artificial, spectacle.” It may “not have been everyone’s cup of tea, but you’ll be hard-pressed to find anyone in attendance that didn’t feel like they got their hard-earned money’s worth” (MOTORSPORT, 11/22).
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1 BUSINESS

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: ‘This isn’t F1’: Max Verstappen criticises overtake-heavy Las Vegas Grand Prix The Guardian
bullets: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix, beating Lando Norris by six-tenths of a second in a race in which the lead changed hands 35 times and there were 352 overtakes. The slipstream-dominated racing resulted from the new regulations, including energy deployment and overtake modes, combined with the circuit's long straights and slow-speed corners.

Verstappen said the racing was not true to Formula One, that it looks great on TV but isn't how it should be, and he again compared it to the video game Mario Kart. Norris said it was probably the best race ever from the outside, though some overtakes were simply pressing boost. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said the race may divide purists, but sponsors who watched told him it was awesome, and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali liked it very much.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Max Verstappen has said his outstanding victory at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday was not really true to the spirit of Formula One and how he wants to race. Verstappen took a remarkable win, defending his lead and retaking it time and time again after it changed hands 35 times in a race dominated by the cars slipstreaming each other for 50 laps.

Verstappen vied with his Red Bull teammate, Isack Hadjar, Mercedes’s George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, and the McLaren of Lando Norris. Each time they would pass him he coolly came back at them to retake the lead.

bullets: Formula 1 is now fully committed to ending the 2026 season in the Middle East, after telling Imola it would not be needed as a plan B. F1 views the MotoGP weekend in Qatar as an example of how the final two Grands Prix, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, can go ahead as planned. Max Verstappen said in the Las Vegas paddock that he would rather stay at home but trusts the safety guarantees.

The four-time world champion said that, given the guarantees offered in private conversations, he has to assume the information is correct and that pushing back is pointless. He still intends to travel, partly because Red Bull has third place in the constructors' championship at stake. Yamaha, with nothing left to fight for, boycotted the MotoGP race in Qatar. Verstappen said the risk may feel closer in the region, but that something could also happen in Las Vegas.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:

Although F1 has always maintained that it would do "the right thing" if the security situation deteriorated, it views the MotoGP weekend in Qatar as an example of how the final two Grands Prix can go ahead as planned.

Max Verstappen has previously made it clear that he always enjoys visiting the Middle East, but that, given the conflicts in the region, he would personally prefer to race elsewhere.

bullets: Liam Lawson set the fastest lap of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, a 1:35.591, the first by a New Zealander in F1 since Denny Hulme at the 1974 Belgian GP. It was the first for Racing Bulls as a constructor, and Lawson became the 142nd driver to set one.

His Racing Bulls car developed a fuel leak before the race and he lost a lap. He finished 15th on the road and was promoted to 14th after Isack Hadjar received a 10-second penalty. Lawson said he did not understand why it took four laps to release him after the safety car, which left him 25 seconds behind the field at the restart.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:

Just prior to the race, where he was due to start in seventh place, Lawson's Racing Bulls machine developed a fuel leak and was wheeled back into the garage for repairs - with the team able to get him back on track, having lost just one lap.

However, running by himself, Lawson was unable to latch onto the field in the slipstream-fest and had an otherwise lonely race, although he was joined briefly by Isack Hadjar's Red Bull after the front-wing failure required a new nose for the Red Bull.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he could win record eighth F1 championship as Ferrari’s number one driver Yahoo News New Zealand

He denied ever asking to be number one, but said that when he was 40 points ahead of Leclerc, the fight was with Kimi Antonelli and he needed the team's backing. His comments followed his second collision with Leclerc in three races, at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, which Fred Vasseur called "completely unacceptable".

Hamilton is 37 points behind Max Verstappen with only 50 points left, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. He is three points clear of George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift. Stewards penalised Leclerc for the Las Vegas collision. Russell finished ninth after hitting the barriers with two laps left while attempting to pass Antonelli.
