Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Salary dispute holding up Ollie Bearman’s new Haas F1 deal Motorsport.com
bullets: Oliver Bearman is the only driver on the F1 grid without a 2027 contract. Motorsport.com understands that the delay concerns the financial terms of his Haas deal, not his long-term future. The sticking point is the salary offered by Haas, which the driver's camp does not consider commensurate with its expectations. Ferrari has already exercised its option to keep him in its driver programme.

Bearman said he is disappointed to have no signed contract at the twentieth round, but ruled out racing elsewhere in 2027, saying there is "zero chance". He said his dream is to race for Ferrari, though he acknowledged there may be challenges. Motorsport.com reports that the matter is expected to be resolved before the Abu Dhabi finale, probably through a financial compromise. Rafael Camara has been announced as his 2027 team-mate.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Motorsport.com understands financial terms are behind the delay in confirming Ollie Bearman for 2027, with Ferrari having already exercised its option on the British driver Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman remains the only driver on the Formula 1 grid without a contract for 2027. It is a situation that would have been hard to imagine just a few weeks ago, given that his retention at Haas had been taken for granted since last summer.

The announcement of Rafael Camara as Bearman's 2027 team-mate, which came ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix, was expected to be swiftly followed by that of his British team-mate. Instead, the silence has dragged on to the point of becoming a talking point, even prompting rumours of Bearman driving elsewhere next year. The paradox is that Bearman and Haas have strong reasons to reach an agreement.

bullets: Sector picked five standout brand activations from the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend, which Oracle Red Bull Racing's Max Verstappen won. Cadillac introduced its F1 project to the local market in the East Harmon Zone, where visitors made personalised scarves and saw vehicles from its high-performance range. LEGO staged an inaugural celebrity race with 11 celebrities, one per team, driving LEGO-built F1 cars, and unveiled a Speed Champions F1 collection covering all 11 teams' 2026 cars and all 22 drivers as minifigures.

Marriott Bonvoy turned the Fountains of Bellagio into a racecourse, where five loyalty members and their guests raced Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli in a speedboat. Vegas has become one of the main races across the season for partnerships to be showcased, with the backdrop of the Strip often used to help catch the eye. Here, in a bumper edition, Sector picks the five standout activations from across the week that demonstrated how those brands are using F1 races to engage fans and tell new stories.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 plans two-team engine supply limit under 2030 V8 rules
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: F1 plans two-team engine supply limit under 2030 V8 rules Autosport
bullets: Formula 1 plans to limit each power unit manufacturer to supplying two teams from 2030, including its own works team, Autosport has learned. The cap sits in the FIA's 2030 framework, which has the unanimous support of the six manufacturers. That framework brings forward the next regulations, with 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 engines, up to 200 kilowatts of electric power and sustainable fuels.

Mercedes supplies McLaren, Williams and Alpine, so two of them would need new suppliers if the FIA World Motor Sport Council approves the plan in Shanghai next month. McLaren CEO Zak Brown said the team has no intention of running anything other than a Mercedes. The FIA's third-party engine proposal is now dead, and the FIA could still oblige a manufacturer to supply a third team.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Formula 1 is planning a shift to just two power unit supplies per manufacturer in 2030, Autosport has learned, raising questions over the status of Mercedes' three current customers.

Over the Las Vegas weekend the FIA announced there was unanimous support to bring the next generation of power unit regulations forward to 2030. That includes a move to 2.1-litre V8 engines, including a turbocharger, a maximum of 200 kilowatts of electric power and the use of sustainable fuels.

bullets: Rafael Camara will keep the Haas seat for the final two Formula 1 grands prix of the season. The 21-year-old Brazilian, already signed to drive for Haas in 2027, was drafted in for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after Esteban Ocon was dropped following a bust-up with team boss Ayao Komatsu.

The decision means Camara will likely lose the Formula 2 title. He leads Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov by seven points with two events left, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Komatsu said the team was excited to finish the season with him, building on his first two race starts in Brazil and America, and that it helps 2027 preparations. Haas's statement carried no quote from Camara.

The decision to keep Camara in the Haas seat in preparation for next season means he will likely lose the Formula 2 title. He is leading the F2 championship by seven points from Bulgarian Nikola Tsolov heading into the final two events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 presses on with Qatar and Abu Dhabi finale despite rising tensions
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: F1 presses on with Qatar and Abu Dhabi finale despite rising tensions Sportsnet.ca
bullets: Formula 1 has decided to keep the original end to the season, finishing in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, despite heightened Middle East tensions linked to the conflict between the United States and Iran. Finishing the season in Las Vegas and adding a stop in Italy were both considered. Earlier this season the Bahrain Grand Prix was moved to Malaysia and the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was cancelled.

The FIA could in theory still cancel the final two races, but the teams are preparing as if they will go ahead. Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss said individual choices must be respected and team safety is paramount. Kimi Antonelli has already won the drivers' title and Mercedes the constructors' title. Max Verstappen, second in the standings, has won four of the past six races, including Las Vegas.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
LAS VEGAS — There was a chance for a short time that the Las Vegas Grand Prix could be the final Formula 1 race of the season. Adding a stop in Italy was also considered. But in the end, F1 officials decided to stay with the original schedule of finishing the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi even with tensions in the Middle East heightened by the conflict between the United States and Iran.

Earlier this season, the Bahrain Grand Prix was moved to Malaysia and the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix canceled. Concerns about a return to a more all-out war are growing after U.S. President Donald Trump said Friday that Iran isn't willing to make a deal he can accept.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: How Antonelli rose so rapidly to become F1 world champion
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: How Antonelli rose so rapidly to become F1 world champion Autosport
bullets: Kimi Antonelli has won the Formula 1 world championship aged 20, clinching the title at the Mexico City Grand Prix at the Foro Sol. He needed two points, qualified fifth and finished third, becoming the youngest champion and the 36th title winner. He took the championship lead in Japan and won from 19th on the grid at Monza, ahead of Mercedes teammate George Russell.

Born in Bologna, he joined Mercedes' driver programme aged 11 and signed to its driver line-up in 2019, with Giovanni Minardi having signed him to management at seven. He won the 2022 Italian F4 title by over 100 points, then the Formula Regional European Championship, and skipped F3 to race in F2 with Prema in 2024. Toto Wolff chose him for 2025 after Lewis Hamilton announced he was leaving Mercedes.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: The one aspect of Max Verstappen "outsmarting" Mercedes that left Red Bull speechless
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: The one aspect of Max Verstappen "outsmarting" Mercedes that left Red Bull speechless Motorsport.com
bullets: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix, his fourth victory in the last six Formula 1 races, at an energy-poor circuit where Red Bull Ford Powertrains had struggled earlier this year. Team principal Laurent Mekies said Verstappen outsmarted the opposition by defending for 50 laps and managing energy and the powerful slipstream.

Mekies said Verstappen deliberately allowed himself to be overtaken a few times to recharge the battery, then counterattacked on the straight towards Turn 1 and later at Turn 3. The Mercedes duo faded late on: George Russell went straight on, while Kimi Antonelli said his power unit became confused when he lifted off the throttle. Mekies said the race gave no clear conclusion on Red Bull's pace at energy-poor tracks.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Photo by: Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images Max Verstappen claimed his fourth victory in the last six Formula 1 Grands Prix. This time, the Dutchman won at what is known as an energy-poor circuit, which is noteworthy given that Red Bull Ford Powertrains was still struggling at such venues at the start of this year.

The victory in Las Vegas appears to underline just how much progress Red Bull has made in that area, although team principal Laurent Mekies believes the result primarily tells a different story. According to him, Verstappen handled the tactical challenges of energy management and the extremely powerful slipstream particularly well.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Verstappen drove a masterclass in Las Vegas to record his third win here and fourth of the season. He led off the line, but was soon challenged by those behind having a tow. Despite losing the lead multiple times, every time the Dutchman kept calm and retook the place. Russell, Norris and Antonelli threw everything they could at the Red Bull man, but no one could make it stick.

Verstappen even had enough composure to debate deployment strategies with the team, worried about being passed last on the final lap and not having time to come back at his rival. But Antonelli’s late issue meant the last lap was the only one where Verstappen had some breathing room from the entire race.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Max Verstappen continues George Russell fallout, labels 2026 F1 season a "complete disaster"
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Max Verstappen continues George Russell fallout, labels 2026 F1 season a "complete disaster" Motorsport.com
bullets: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix and then criticised George Russell, saying he enjoyed that Russell had "absolutely no chance" after the Mercedes driver went straight on and lost his chance of victory. Verstappen said Russell was "beaten at every corner", a reference to him deliberately letting himself be passed several times on the Strip to recharge his battery. He then fought back at Turn 1 or Turn 3. He called Russell's 2026 season a "complete disaster".

The row began with a clash in third free practice, which ended with a warning for Verstappen. Russell later told Sky Sports Italy he would not accept someone treating him that way. Verstappen said the comments gave him no extra motivation because Russell is "nowhere near my level". Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said the rivalry caused "zero" distraction for the team. Motorsport.com compared the row with the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix media day two years ago, when Verstappen called Russell a "backstabber".
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Verstappen says he enjoyed watching Russell get "beaten at every corner" in Las Vegas. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies adds that the rivalry is not a distraction While the clash between Max Verstappen and George Russell during the third free practice session for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix appeared to have been settled with a warning for the Red Bull driver, the dispute has since escalated in the media.

Speaking to Sky Sports Italy after qualifying, Russell made it clear that he was no longer willing to accept "somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else."

Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Verstappen wins in Las Vegas] and criticises Russell, calling the Mercedes driver's 2026 season a "complete disaster" after their practice clash.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Hadjar penalised after backing up Russell in Las Vegas GP, Perez given grid drop for Qatar GP
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Hadjar penalised after backing up Russell in Las Vegas GP, Perez given grid drop for Qatar GP Autosport
bullets: Isack Hadjar received a 10-second penalty in Formula 1's Las Vegas Grand Prix for driving unnecessarily slowly under the safety car. The race was neutralised on lap 19 after Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara collided. Stewards found Hadjar was about 100km/h slower than team-mate Max Verstappen at one point, to allow Red Bull a double-stack pitstop. The penalty moved him from 14th to 15th, after his front wing broke at the restart.

Perez was given a five-place grid penalty for the Qatar Grand Prix for the collision with Camara, which broke the suspension on Camara's Cadillac. Stewards ruled that Perez had not earned the right to the corner and was wholly to blame. In the Hadjar case, they cited the precedent of Lando Norris at the 2023 Canadian Grand Prix.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Isack Hadjar has received a 10-second penalty for driving unnecessarily slowly in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix – the result of his actions under the safety car. The race was neutralised on lap 19 when Sergio Perez and Rafael Camara collided; Max Verstappen was leading team-mate Hadjar but the Red Bulls and Mercedes cars lay within just over a second; the double-stack meant Hadjar risked losing track position to Russell and other drivers.

The Frenchman therefore slowed down, to the extent that he was 4.288s slower than his team-mate on that lap. This mitigated the effect of the double-stack, though he still couldn’t retain second position.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Hadjar given 10-second penalty] for backing up Russell under the safety car in Las Vegas, while Perez gets a five-place Qatar grid drop.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.angle: Stewards' rulings set precedents on safety-car tactics that will apply at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, where Yas Marina's pit-lane layout could make double-stacking relevant.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Hamilton-Leclerc collision completely unacceptable, says Ferrari boss
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in Las Vegas.
bullets: Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur called the collision between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc in the Las Vegas Grand Prix "completely unacceptable". Leclerc tipped Hamilton into a spin with 22 laps to go and received a 10-second penalty, finishing 10th, three places behind Hamilton. Max Verstappen of Red Bull won the race, and McLaren finished on the podium.

It was the second race-compromising incident between the pair, after their first-lap fight in Mexico cost them a win and a meeting to clear the air at the previous race in Brazil. Vasseur said he would speak to the drivers the day after the race. Hamilton said he had never asked to be number one and that the question "should be for Ferrari now", while Leclerc said they needed to "fix whatever is not working".
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc face yet another tense discussion over their ability to race together cleanly on track after colliding in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Leclerc tipped Hamilton into a spin with 22 laps to go, costing both points in a race where at one stage they were racing with the McLarens, who finished on the podium. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for the incident, which meant he finished 10th, three places behind Hamilton, in a race won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Ferrari's Vasseur calls Hamilton-Leclerc collision] "completely unacceptable" after Leclerc's penalty in the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.angle: Ferrari's internal driver tensions are a team matter with no direct link to ADNOC or the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, but they shape the title narrative heading into the season finale.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Charles Leclerc: Ferrari must find fix to 'unacceptable' feud after Lewis Hamilton clash
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Charles Leclerc: Ferrari must find fix to 'unacceptable' feud after Lewis Hamilton clash Motorsport.com
bullets: Charles Leclerc finished the Las Vegas Grand Prix sixth on the road but was demoted to 10th after a 10-second penalty for an avoidable collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton. On lap 38 he went up the inside at Turn 7, rode the kerb and clipped Hamilton's right-rear wheel, spinning him. Team principal Frederic Vasseur told him over the radio to report to him straight after the race.

Leclerc called the situation with Hamilton unacceptable and said Ferrari needed to fix whatever was not working. The pair also clashed in Mexico, where their first-lap fight let Max Verstappen win. Both drivers had said they held productive clear-the-air talks before the Las Vegas event.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Photo by: Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images Charles Leclerc ended the Las Vegas with a 10-second penalty for an avoidable collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton – and a telling-off from team boss Frederic Vasseur ringing in his ears.

Both Ferraris had started outside the top 10, having failed to orchestrate the necessary slipstream in qualifying, but then made progress in an opening phase of a race characterised by the kind of extreme 'yo-yo' overtaking rarely seen since the beginning of the season. Whenever Leclerc and Hamilton are running in close proximity on track, arguments are sure to follow, and the first rumblings began when Leclerc took to the radio to say "He [Hamilton] needs to be careful with the squeezing" as they duelled with McLaren's Oscar Piastri in the lower reaches of the top 10.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Leclerc penalised for Hamilton collision] in Las Vegas, dropping from sixth to 10th as Ferrari's internal tension continues.

She started from pole after the biggest qualifying margin in F1 Academy history and held off Alba Larsen in a race-long duel. The race was the 14th and final round of the 2026 season, with the title already decided. It was also the last appearance in the series for several drivers reaching the two-season limit. A Safety Car was deployed on lap nine after contact between Lloyd and Robertson, and the field restarted on lap 10, with Palmowski and Larsen controlling the front.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: “My mistake was to lift” – Why Antonelli lost power in Las Vegas GP victory battle
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: “My mistake was to lift” – Why Antonelli lost power in Las Vegas GP victory battle Autosport
bullets: Kimi Antonelli says a mistake on the penultimate lap cost him a chance of winning the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he finished fourth. The Mercedes driver started sixth after a five-place engine-change penalty and dropped two places on lap one on mediums. He recovered to challenge pole-sitter Max Verstappen, and the two traded the lead repeatedly, with Antonelli 0.001s ahead on the line on lap 43 of 50.

Antonelli explained that he lifted before Turn 14 to keep overtake mode and stay behind Verstappen. The lift triggered the system, so he exited the corner with no battery and lost almost two seconds on the straight, and both McLarens passed him. He said Mercedes could keep up with Red Bull on the straights, and that he enjoyed the 'yo-yo' racing despite its stress.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Kimi Antonelli has explained the quirky “mistake” that cost him a shot at Formula 1 victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The fastest driver in qualifying, Antonelli was sixth on the grid owing to a five-place drop for an engine change and was the only top-10 starter on mediums rather than softs, which contributed to a further two-position drop on lap one.

The new world champion recovered to fourth by lap 17 and went on to challenge polesitter Max Verstappen and Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the second half of the race, emerging as the Red Bull’s main rival late on.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Antonelli says a lift cost him] victory chance in Las Vegas, finishing fourth after losing battery on the penultimate lap.

bullets: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix, his fourth win of the season after Bahrain, Singapore and Mexico, and his ninth consecutive podium. Mercedes' George Russell crashed out of second on lap 48 while trying to pass team-mate Kimi Antonelli, dropping to ninth. Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri completed the podium for McLaren.

bullets: George Russell said he made "a high-risk move" when he crashed on lap 48 of 50 in the Las Vegas Grand Prix while trying to win. He dived down the inside of Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, locked up and hit the wall. He recovered to finish ninth, and said he would have taken third if he had been conservative.

Russell and polesitter Max Verstappen traded the lead repeatedly, with Russell leading on at least six occasions, as the new power units' battery and energy deployment produced 'yo-yo' racing. Russell is now fourth in the drivers' championship, level on points with fifth-placed Lando Norris. He is three points behind Lewis Hamilton and 40 behind runner-up Verstappen.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
George Russell has admitted to making “a high-risk move” after crashing with three laps remaining in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in an attempt to clinch victory. As ‘yo-yo’ racing returned to F1, polesitter Max Verstappen and Russell frequently traded the lead throughout the race, occasionally challenged by the sister cars of Isack Hadjar in the first half of the race and Kimi Antonelli later on.

On lap 48 of 50, Russell had dropped down to third behind Verstappen and Antonelli and dived down the inside of his team-mate’s Silver Arrow, but locked up and hit the wall. Minimal damage meant he was able to finish the race, albeit down in ninth.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Verstappen wins extraordinary race as Ferraris collide
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Red Bull's Max Verstappen wins an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes and another collision between the Ferraris.
bullets: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix after a race featuring 34 lead changes. He started from pole and repeatedly traded the lead with Mercedes' George Russell and Kimi Antonelli. Lando Norris finished second, and both McLarens passed Antonelli around the outside of the final corner heading into the last lap.

Russell locked his brakes and hit the barrier going for a move at Turn Five with two laps left, and he finished ninth. At Ferrari, Charles Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for tipping Lewis Hamilton into a spin, after Hamilton had earlier been given his own 10-second penalty for passing Norris off the track. Formula 1 now moves to the Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit from 27-29 November.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an extraordinary Las Vegas Grand Prix that featured 34 lead changes in a non-stop battle at the front. The leading group of 10 cars were tied together for the vast majority of the race as the lead constantly changed hands between Verstappen and the Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.

But Verstappen was the one constant, always seeming a step ahead of his rivals as he debated electrical energy deployment strategy with his team. And in the final laps Mercedes' challenge unravelled as first Russell made a mistake and crashed trying to pass Antonelli, and the Italian lost out to the two McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri going into the final lap.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Verstappen wins Las Vegas Grand Prix] from pole after 34 lead changes, with Norris second and Russell ninth after a late crash.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.angle: Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the Qatar Grand Prix on 27-29 November, ahead of the season finale at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Max Verstappen cemented his place in second in the drivers' standings with a win in the Las Vegas Grand Prix as George Russell could only finish in ninth. Russell dropped out of contention late on after hitting the wall when trying to pass Kimi Antonelli for second, and eventually dropped to ninth.

It means Verstappen now moves to 40 points clear of Russell whilst Lewis Hamilton moves ahead of Russell into third place in the drivers'. In the constructors', McLaren's two-three result through Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri was enough to reduce Red Bull's lead in the fight for third.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Lewis Hamilton questions stewards in unaired radio message after F1 Vegas penalty
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Lewis Hamilton questions stewards in unaired radio message after F1 Vegas penalty Motorsport.com
bullets: Lewis Hamilton questioned FIA stewarding consistency in a team radio message not shown on the global feed, after a 10-second penalty at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. He started 11th and was penalised around lap 13 for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage while battling Lando Norris at the Turn 7-8 chicane.

Hamilton said that when others get mitigating circumstances they receive five seconds, while he received 10. This appeared to refer to Charles Leclerc's five-second penalty at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November, which stewards halved citing mitigation. The FIA plans to begin phasing in full-time Formula 1 stewards in 2027.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond. Lewis Hamilton’s recovery drive at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix hit a major snag in the opening half of the race - and prompted a pointed complaint over Ferrari team radio regarding FIA stewarding consistency.

Starting 11th after both Ferraris were eliminated in Q2 on Friday night, Hamilton climbed into the points during a fiercely contested opening stint alongside team-mate Charles Leclerc and McLaren’s Lando Norris. Around Lap 13, while fighting for seventh place through the Turn 7–8 chicane, Hamilton ran into the run-off area and cut the corner while duelling Norris.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Cadillac Has Confirmed Its 2027 F1 Drivers, but There’s Far More Uncertainty to Clear Up
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Cadillac Has Confirmed Its 2027 F1 Drivers, but There’s Far More Uncertainty to Clear Up Sports Illustrated
bullets: Cadillac has confirmed Valtteri Bottas will stay for the 2027 Formula 1 season, ending weeks of speculation, with the announcement made on the Wednesday before the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The team enters the weekend scoreless after 20 races and last among 11 teams. Its best 2026 result was Bottas's 13th place at the Chinese Grand Prix, and the drivers have had 15 DNFs in 39 race entries. Cadillac sits seven points behind Aston Martin and 12 behind Williams.

Sergio Pérez said the team expected to be sharper operationally, citing a 9.68-second pit stop in Brazil, and called for a stronger team culture. Team principal Graeme Lowden was replaced by Marcin Budkowski in August. Mark Walter, owner of TWG Motorsport, is exploring a sale of his stake, and Sportico reported he is seeking a $3 billion valuation. Cadillac has also said it intends to become a full works team with its own power units by the end of the decade.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
LAS VEGAS — A critical piece of the puzzle for the 2027 Formula One season fell into place on the Wednesday ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix when Cadillac announced that Valtteri Bottas would return to the team for another season. The announcement ended weeks of speculation that the veteran driver could be on his way out amid struggles in races throughout the 2026 campaign.

Alas, the team ultimately chose to carry on with Bottas. That’s one question answered for Cadillac. But the laundry list of others looms large as F1’s newest team stumbles its way to the end of its inaugural season.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Junior drivers to the fore on sensational FIA World Cup Saturday in Macau
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Junior drivers to the fore on sensational FIA World Cup Saturday in Macau Federation Internationale de l'Automobile
bullets: Emirati driver Rashid Al Dhaheri won the Qualification Race for the FIA FR World Cup at Macau on the penultimate day of Macau Grand Prix week. His R-ace GP team-mate Kenzo Craigie won the equivalent race for the FIA F4 World Cup. Both are members of the Mercedes Junior Programme, and the racing took place on the Guia Circuit.

Conditions were warm and dry after Friday's rain. In the GT category, Laurin Heinrich converted pole position, secured by winning Friday's Superpole shootout, into victory in the FIA GT World Cup Qualification Race. He drove a Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) (Evo) for AO by Absolute and earned the Pirelli Pole Position Award for the FIA GT World Cup Main Race on Sunday.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
FIA junior single-seater stars Rashid Al Dhaheri and Kenzo Craigie were triumphant during the penultimate day of Macau Grand Prix week, with Laurin Heinrich also emerging as a big winner after Friday’s rain gave way to more traditional warm and dry conditions on the legendary Guia Circuit.

Members of the Mercedes Junior Programme, the R-ace GP team-mates Al Dhaheri and Craigie won the Qualification Race for the FIA FR World Cup and FIA F4 World Cup respectively, as Heinrich converted pole position – secured by winning Friday’s Superpole qualifying shootout – into victory in the FIA GT World Cup Qualification Race driving a Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) (Evo) for AO by Absolute.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Macau GP: Rashid Al Dhaheri defeats Mattia Colnaghi to take qualification race win
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Macau GP: Rashid Al Dhaheri defeats Mattia Colnaghi to take qualification race win Motorsport.com
bullets: Rashid Al Dhaheri won the Macau Grand Prix qualification race, passing polesitter Alex Ninovic at the start and holding off a final-lap attack from Mattia Colnaghi. Al Dhaheri, who drives for R-ace GP and finished fourth in this year's Formula Regional European Championship, led before the first turn. Colnaghi, a Red Bull Junior driving for MP Motorsport, crossed the line 0.251s behind.

Ninovic finished about 3s behind Al Dhaheri in third, ahead of Enzo Deligny of Pinnacle Motorsport in fourth. Colnaghi will start from the front row for Sunday's main race. The qualifying sessions had been heavily disrupted, with five red flags on Thursday and a rain-affected Q2 on Friday. The race itself was relatively incident-free, with the only significant clash coming when Taito Kato hit Kabir Anurag on the third lap.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Rashid Al Dhaheri took victory in the Macau Grand Prix qualification race after jumping polesitter Alex Ninovic at the start and resisting a final-lap attack from Mattia Colnaghi.

Rodin racer Ninovic had set the pace during a heavily disrupted opening qualifying session on Thursday that featured five red flags, before Friday's Q2 was rain-affected, but the Australian did not make a great launch from pole and was instantly under pressure from Al Dhaheri.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Verstappen responds to Russell after Las Vegas GP practice clash over 'gentleman's agreement'
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Verstappen responds to Russell after Las Vegas GP practice clash over 'gentleman's agreement' Autosport
bullets: Max Verstappen has dismissed his clash with George Russell in final practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix. He told Dutch media he did not want to waste his time on it and that it was "not worth it to me at all". The two made contact at Turn 14 after Verstappen overtook Russell, slowed and, according to the stewards, changed direction several times, and Russell went down the inside. Stewards gave Verstappen a warning, which carries no penalty.

Asked about the so-called "gentleman's agreement", Verstappen said he had never seen such an agreement in his life. The stewards noted that drivers are expected to keep position on preparation laps, but said informal understandings were of limited relevance and that the cars' movements and relative positions were decisive. After qualifying, Verstappen said "nothing happened" and that the clash gave him no extra motivation to keep Russell behind on the grid. They share the front row after Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position Motorsport.com
bullets: Max Verstappen took pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix with a 1m34.151s, 0.073s ahead of Mercedes' George Russell on 1m34.224s. Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with 1m33.893s but drops to sixth on the grid after a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes' updated ADUO turbocharger.

Toto Wolff said Russell had the perfect position, four seconds behind the car in front, and that Mercedes must find out whether a mistake at Turns 7 to 9 or something else cost him pole. Russell, third in the standings and 17 points behind Verstappen, starts second after both Ferraris were knocked out in Q2. Verstappen received an FIA warning after a Turn 14 clash with Russell in final practice.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Las Vegas GP pole by 0.073s to Max Verstappen despite ideal track position For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

Mercedes left Friday night qualifying at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit with the fastest car on track, yet team principal Toto Wolff still had questions to answer. World champion Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with a 1m33.893s, only to drop to sixth on the grid due to a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes’ updated ADUO turbocharger. Instead of team-mate George Russell inheriting pole, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen snatched top spot with a 1m34.151s - edging Russell’s 1m34.224s by just 0.073 seconds.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Verstappen takes Las Vegas pole] by 0.073s from George Russell, with Antonelli sixth after a five-place penalty.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: REVERSE GRID RACE: Alba Larsen charges from ninth to claim second victory of 2026 in Las Vegas F1 Academy
bullets: Alba Larsen won the F1 Academy Reverse Grid Race in Las Vegas, her second victory of 2026, after starting ninth. It is the lowest winning grid position on record. The Ferrari driver took the lead on Lap 5 and held off 2026 Champion Alisha Palmowski through two Safety Car interruptions, with Megan Bruce third.

Campos Racing now lead MP Motorsport by 52 points in the Teams' standings as they chase their first Teams' title. The final race of the 2026 season, the Feature Race, starts on Sunday at 16:20 local time (UTC−8), with Palmowski on pole. The Teams' title and second place in the Drivers' standings are still undecided.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Alba Larsen claimed her second F1 ACADEMY victory with a remarkable recovery from ninth on the grid in Las Vegas, holding off 2026 Champion Alisha Palmowski in a dramatic Reverse Grid Race.

The Ferrari driver seized the lead after an eventful opening five laps and resisted Palmowski’s late challenge following two Safety Car interruptions, setting a new record for the lowest winning grid position. Megan Bruce completed the podium in third to strengthen Campos Racing’s position in the Teams’ title fight.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 Broadcasters Announce Bad News for Qatar Grand Prix Amid Middle East Conflicts
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: F1 Broadcasters Announce Bad News for Qatar Grand Prix Amid Middle East Conflicts Yahoo Sports
bullets: Sky Germany will not send an editorial team to the Qatar Grand Prix at Lusail International Circuit on 27-29 November, citing security concerns in the Middle East. Its commentary will come from Unterföhring, near Munich, with pre-race coverage starting 60 minutes before the race. According to SID, ServusTV in Austria, Canal+ in France and DAZN's Spanish operation also plan to work without on-site crews. Sky UK and Sky Italia are reported to be considering their options, but neither has confirmed a withdrawal.

Sky Germany currently intends to send a crew to the Abu Dhabi season finale at Yas Marina Circuit on 4-6 December, but says staff safety is its priority and it will keep monitoring developments. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff urged people to trust F1 and the FIA rather than social media, and said no employee will be obliged to travel. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said: "We are ready for Qatar and Abu Dhabi." Both races remain on the calendar.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Formula 1 is facing an unusual broadcasting situation ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, with several television networks opting against sending their crews to the Lusail International Circuit amid security concerns in the Middle East. Sky Germany has confirmed that it will produce its coverage remotely, while other broadcasters are also expected to follow a similar approach.

Sky Deutschland confirmed to the German Sport-Informations-Dienst (SID) that it would not send an editorial team to Qatar for the November 27-29 race weekend. "We have decided to forego an editorial team on site," the broadcaster said. Its commentary will instead come from Unterföhring, near Munich, with pre-race coverage beginning 60 minutes before the Grand Prix.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Broadcasters skip Qatar GP travel] over Middle East security, while Sky Germany still plans to attend Abu Dhabi on 4-6 December.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.angle: Broadcaster attendance at the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix finale is undecided for at least Sky Germany, which bears on media coverage of an ADNOC-founded event.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Russell fastest in final practice after Verstappen collision
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: F1 Las Vegas GP: Russell fastest in final practice after Verstappen collision Autosport
bullets: George Russell topped the timesheets in the third and final practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, setting a 1m34.041s in his Mercedes. Kimi Antonelli demoted Lando Norris to third, with Charles Leclerc fourth and Franco Colapinto fifth for Alpine. Both Thursday sessions had been derailed by rain, so Friday's session was the only dry running before qualifying and the race, in 14C temperatures on the 6.2km Strip circuit. Russell had declined a Mercedes turbo upgrade to avoid a grid penalty.

Russell and Max Verstappen collided at the end of the session when Russell went down the inside of Turn 14 to re-pass the Red Bull, making side-on contact. The incident was to be investigated by the FIA's stewards. Earlier, Verstappen had locked up into the runoff area, prompting Norris to say "Instant karma, amazing" on team radio. Liam Lawson was seventh, followed by Lewis Hamilton, Pierre Gasly and Arvid Lindblad.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
George Russell collided with Max Verstappen in a tense third practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as the Mercedes Formula 1 driver topped the timesheets. After both of Thursday's practice sessions had been derailed by rain, the Las Vegas Strip was buzzing with activity at dusk on Friday. The sole remaining practice session became crucial as it presented the only dry running heading into qualifying and the race, as all 22 cars sprinted out of the pitlane in short order.

Amid chilly 14C temperatures, the Thursday rainfall only made the 6.2km circuit around the Las Vegas Strip even more difficult to drive, with surface grip extremely limited. Verstappen survived a sideways scare and steering rack issues to lead the early running with a 1m35.675s on soft tyres, by far the most popular tyre in cold conditions as it was easier to fire up to temperature.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Russell fastest in final Las Vegas practice] with a 1m34.041s lap, after colliding with Verstappen at Turn 14.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: FSG Let Exclusive Window to Buy Mark Walter’s F1 Team Lapse
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: FSG Let Exclusive Window to Buy Mark Walter’s F1 Team Lapse Front Office Sports
bullets: Fenway Sports Group had an exclusive window to agree a deal for Mark Walter's stake in the Cadillac Formula 1 team but let it lapse, Front Office Sports has learned. Two sources said FSG remains in talks, though the discussions have hit a snag. Walter has been seeking at least $3 billion for the stake.

Walter's company, TWG Global, said in late August that the team was not for sale, but Sportico reported on 2 November that it was on the market, with at least seven interested buyers including FSG. FSG owns the Red Sox, Liverpool and RFK Racing. Walter has sold the Lakers at a $12.5 billion valuation and exited Chelsea and Strasbourg, but he has said he will not sell the Dodgers.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Fenway Sports Group had an exclusive window to reach a deal for Mark Walter’s stake in the Cadillac Formula One team but let it lapse, Front Office Sports has learned. Despite no longer having exclusivity, FSG isn’t out of the running and is in fact still in talks, but those discussions have hit a snag, two sources tell FOS.

Walter’s company, TWG Global, said in late August that the F1 team was not for sale, but by the beginning of this month that had changed. Sportico reported on Nov. 2 that Walter had put the team on the market, was asking for at least $3 billion, and that at least seven buyers were interested, including FSG. The identities of the other potential buyers involved in talks have not been reported. The two sources tell FOS Walter has been seeking at least $3 billion.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.label: F1 BUSINESS
Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [FSG let exclusivity lapse] on Mark Walter's Cadillac F1 stake, with talks continuing and a $3 billion asking price.

bullets: Apple, the exclusive US broadcast partner of Formula 1, has added US rights to F1 Academy, the all-female racing series, starting in 2027. Apple TV will cover every F1 Academy qualifying session and race each season, alongside in-depth programming and exclusive original content, with customisable features for following drivers and the championship.

F1 Academy will feature at seven Grands Prix in 2027, including Jeddah, Shanghai, Montreal, Silverstone and Budapest, before the final two US rounds in Austin and Las Vegas. Apple secured a five-year exclusive US F1 deal from 2026, valued at around $140 million. Managing director Susie Wolff said the deal reflects the series' growing US momentum. Nike and Standard Chartered also join as sponsors from 2027.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Athletic apparel giant Nike has joined F1 as its official partner and uniform supplier, taking over from Puma at the start of 2027. As was long rumoured, Nike will start supplying F1 personnel with apparel and footwear from the start of next season, a partnership that also extends to F1 Academy, which had both been using Puma kit until this year.

The athletic company will also come up with F1-inspired retail collections, the first of which will go on sale on Friday and be centred around the Las Vegas Grand Prix. "Nike will bring new energy to the pinnacle of motorsport through capsule collections with a focus on style, performance, and lifestyle including footwear, apparel, and accessories, as well as performance innovations, and race-weekend experiences for the next generation of athletes and fans," the announcement promised.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: "It was scary at 100km/h" - F1 drivers shocked by Las Vegas 'ice rink'
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: "It was scary at 100km/h" - F1 drivers shocked by Las Vegas 'ice rink' Motorsport.com
bullets: Rain disrupted Thursday's opening practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with first practice a complete wash and no driver setting a lap time. In second practice, drivers started on full wets before moving to intermediates as a dry line formed, and every driver kept clear of the barriers on the low-grip street circuit. Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad likened it to an ice rink and called driving at 100km/h in a slow corner scary.

Alex Albon said it was the lowest-grip track of the year, and Oscar Piastri said the start was close to impossible. After first practice Pirelli raised its full wet tyre blanket temperature from 40C to 60C, which Albon felt did not go far enough. Isack Hadjar said he enjoyed the intermediates. Pirelli plans to introduce updated wet tyres as early as next season.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
With rain affecting Thursday's Las Vegas Grand Prix running on the low-grip street circuit around the Strip, the biggest takeaway was not who was fastest, but the impressive fact that every Formula 1 driver kept it out of the barriers.

Following F1's first proper wet weekend of the year in Brazil, using both the full wets and intermediates tyres in qualifying and race conditions, drivers were concerned over how Pirelli's wet weather range would work on a circuit without high-speed corners, where tyres are much harder to get up to temperature.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.line: [Rain and low grip at Las Vegas] left F1 drivers struggling on wet tyres, though none hit the barriers on Thursday.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Pirelli reintroduces stint limit for F1 Qatar GP
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Pirelli reintroduces stint limit for F1 Qatar GP Motorsport.com
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Formula 1 teams will again have to follow a prescribed stint limit for each car at the Qatar Grand Prix to protect the Pirelli tyres around the high-degradation track. Drivers must complete no more than 27 laps per stint at Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will likely opt for a two-stop strategy in the 57-lap race.

It is a similar situation to last year when stints were limited to 25 laps following analysis of the 2024 contest, where “several tyres, particularly the left front, had reached the maximum wear”. The 2023 event was also the subject of stint limits, though that year, the enforced limit was just 18 laps.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: Palmowski makes history as she secures pole in Las Vegas
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Palmowski makes history as she secures pole in Las Vegas Formula 1
bullets: Red Bull Racing's Alisha Palmowski took pole position for the F1 Academy Las Vegas Feature Race, her seventh pole of the season, in her final F1 Academy qualifying session. Her 2m 9.915s lap gave her the largest qualifying margin of her season and the largest in series history. Emma Felbermayr was second, 1.578s behind, with Alba Larsen a further 1.671s back in third.

Audi driver Larsen's team-mate position changed after Felbermayr's penalties: Larsen was promoted to second on the grid after two three-place penalties dropped another driver to fifth, and Megan Bruce moved into the top three. Nina Gademan will start fourth. Mathilda Paatz starts on pole for the Reverse Grid Race, set for 18:15 local time on Saturday.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Red Bull Racing's Alisha Palmowski secured pole position for the F1 ACADEMY Las Vegas Feature Race. Alisha Palmowski delivered in her final F1 ACADEMY Qualifying session, leading from the halfway mark to take her seventh pole position of the season by the largest margin in the series' history.

The Red Bull Racing driver was untouchable through the second half of the 30-minute session, after topping the timesheets during the afternoon wet Practice session. After setting an initial benchmark lap time, Palmowski took a firm grip at the top of the timesheets with a 2m 9.915s effort to set her largest margin in a Qualifying session.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 bosses close to V8 engines deal from 2030
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Formula 1 bosses are close to a deal that will see V8 turbo hybrid engines replace the current controversial engines in 2030.
bullets: Formula 1 bosses are close to agreeing that 2.1-litre V8 turbo hybrid engines will replace the current power units in 2030. McLaren CEO Zak Brown said an agreement in principle had been reached, though some details remain unresolved. The electrical element will be capped at 200kW, down from 350kW this year, with only half available at all times and the rest reserved for overtake mode.

The combustion engine will produce about 780bhp, giving roughly 1,050bhp in overtake mode. Engines will carry a budget cap of $190m a year and a 150kg weight limit. General Motors will delay its Cadillac engine to 2030 and be classed as a new manufacturer, while the team uses Ferrari customer engines through 2029. The rules are a compromise after FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem initially pushed for naturally aspirated engines.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Formula 1 bosses are close to a deal that will see V8 turbo hybrid engines replace the current controversial engines in 2030. McLaren chief executive officer Zak Brown said an "agreement in principle" had been reached by engine manufacturers and F1 bosses on the new rules.

These will be for a 2.1-litre V8 turbo engine with a smaller electrical element than this year, as first revealed by BBC Sport last month. Some details remain to be resolved but the main core of the rules has been agreed.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Cadillac scraps V6 F1 engine, delays entry as PU manufacturer Motorsport.com
bullets: Cadillac will delay the introduction of its in-house F1 power unit by a year to 2030, having planned to use a General Motors engine from 2029. CEO Dan Towriss confirmed the team will remain a Ferrari customer through 2029 and bring its own unit online in 2030 with the V8. The change follows an agreement in principle on bringing forward V8 engines.

Towriss said Cadillac supports the V8 direction set under the FIA's leadership. The team's dedicated power unit facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, opens on 18 December. Cadillac will initially work on both V6 and V8 designs, though the current-generation unit will no longer need full development for 2029.

CEO Dan Towriss says Cadillac will remain a Ferrari customer team for another year. General Motors has postponed the introduction of its own F1 power unit until the arrival of the V8 in 2030

Cadillac is set to delay the introduction of its in-house Formula 1 power unit by a year to 2030. The American squad's initial plan was to compete in the championship with its own General Motors power unit for the first time in 2029. However, that was based on the idea that the current regulations cycle would run its full course and that the next generation of power units would not be introduced until 2031.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: ‘I’m part of a family’ – Mercedes’ first female junior Fluxa Cross on her F1 ACADEMY debut and Silver Arrows support
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: ‘I’m part of a family’ – Mercedes’ first female junior Fluxa Cross on her F1 ACADEMY debut and Silver Arrows support Formula 1
bullets: Mercedes junior Luna Fluxa Cross, 16, makes her F1 Academy debut in Las Vegas as the Wild Card entry for Round 6, driving for Hitech. She races in the Spanish F4 Championship this season and faces a new car, new tyres, her first street circuit and jet lag.

She joined the Mercedes-AMG F1 Junior Programme in 2022 aged 11, the first female driver to do so, and is now its longest-standing junior. In 2024 she became the first female winner of an FIA international championship since 1966, taking the OK-N Senior title by 125 points. She said Mercedes have helped with training, nutrition and mindset, and that a strong weekend matters for winning a seat next year. Nine Wild Cards have earned full-time seats since 2024.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Mercedes junior Luna Fluxa Cross reflects on how she is feeling ahead of her F1 ACADEMY debut in Las Vegas. Luna Fluxa Cross has been one of the most talked about up-and-coming female drivers for the past few years. Now the Mercedes junior is preparing for the biggest stage of her career so far as she makes her F1 ACADEMY debut on the streets of Las Vegas.

Fluxa Cross is competing as the Wild Card entry for Round 6, a one-off appearance created to strengthen the talent pool in the regions where the all-female series races. Competing in the Spanish F4 Championship this season, the 16-year-old faces a steep learning curve. She needs to adapt to a new car, a new team in Hitech and new tyres alongside racing on a street circuit for the first time. On top of that comes the jet lag that challenges every driver on an overseas round.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: F1 to introduce full-time race stewards from 2027
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season.
bullets: Formula 1's governing body, the FIA, will introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season, following repeated calls from drivers who criticised inconsistent penalty decisions for on-track incidents. It will begin recruiting and plans a "phased introduction" during 2027, with a small number of full-time stewards recruited that year and the group expanded from 2028.

The FIA said existing stewards will continue in a mixed roster of full-time and part-time officials, and that driver stewards, usually former drivers, will remain. Each grand prix currently has four stewards, one of them an ex-driver. The move follows the opening of an FIA race operations centre at F1's Biggin Hill headquarters. President Mohammed Ben Sulayem called it a significant step towards a dedicated officiating ecosystem. Carlos Sainz, a Grand Prix Drivers' Association director, said last year that at least two of three stewards should be permanent.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Formula 1's governing body the FIA is to introduce permanent race stewards from the 2027 season. The move follows consistent calls from grand prix drivers for the change because of criticisms of inconsistency of decisions regarding penalties for on-track incidents.

The FIA said in a statement that it would begin recruiting permanent stewards, and was planning a "phased introduction" during the 2027 season. The FIA statement added: "The introduction of dedicated full-time stewards to the FIA's flagship championship will provide continuity and expertise within the stewarding structure, further advancing the FIA's commitment to fairness through the ongoing review and continuous improvement of sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines.

bullets: Max Verstappen told ESPN he "stresses a bit less" after winning several titles. He is second in the 2026 championship behind new champion Kimi Antonelli with three races left. He has won in Malaysia, Singapore and Mexico City this season, after Red Bull struggled early on and major upgrades brought them back. Last year's title fight went to the Abu Dhabi finale, where Lando Norris was crowned champion, 12 points ahead of Verstappen.

Verstappen, 29, had raised the possibility of retiring at the end of 2026 after criticising the new regulations. He said he still loves racing and has a contract until 2030. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has hinted that V8 engines could return in 2030. Verstappen named the Nürburgring 24 Hours and Le Mans hypercars as races he would like to enter, but gave no timeframe. His team retired from the Nürburgring 24 Hours in May with a driveshaft problem. He ruled out running a top-level team that would require constant travel.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Max Verstappen spent four years making winning in Formula 1 look almost routine. But after two seasons without a world championship, the Red Bull driver has found himself on the other side of a title fight -- and discovered that losing doesn't weigh quite as heavily as it once might have.

The Verstappen of 2021 was desperate for a world crown after five seasons at Red Bull in which he had proved his star quality but never quite had the car to match. The Verstappen of 2026? Even a difficult start to the season -- one that had him seriously questioning his future -- hasn't stopped him finding his way back to the front.

Camara is confirmed to race for Haas in 2027, but has not decided whether to contest the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi or return to Formula 2.

Camara said he expects to be calmer in Las Vegas because he has had more time to prepare than for his last-minute call-up in Brazil. He said he would discuss the final two races with his team after the Las Vegas weekend and would be happy with either option. He added that Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu had not complained about anything on his debut weekend, though Camara felt he could have done some things better on the Sunday.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Future imperfect: What's behind the abortive 2030 F1 rules announcement? Famously, when the papal conclave gathers to elect a new pope, a successful vote is communicated to the huddled masses via smoke from the Sistine Chapel chimney as the chemically impregnated ballot papers are burned: white smoke signifies a decision, black means yet another round of voting. The practice derives from the 13th century, when the cardinals took three years to debate a successor to Clement IV, prompting the frustrated local faithful to lock them inside the palace with only bread and water to subsist upon.

All this came to mind when Monday's much-anticipated meeting between the engine manufacturers, the FIA and the commercial rights holder to discuss the next generation of Formula 1 engines was followed by the 21st century F1 equivalent of white smoke billowing from the chimney: an Instagram post by FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem.

bullets: McLaren followed two consecutive constructors' titles with a difficult 2026 season, but team principal Andrea Stella says it has returned to the front. He gave three causes: a development delay of about three months at the start of the season, the 2025 title fight with Red Bull slowing work on the 2026 car, and the team's status as a Mercedes customer.

Stella said McLaren arrived late on engine power curves, cooling and integration. Mercedes withheld some proprietary optimisation software, and McLaren will only have full access in 2027. He said no top-team upgrades failed, the Miami and Hungary upgrades gave clear gains, and the team now uses the power unit far better. He added that McLaren cannot accept third or fourth place as good enough.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
McLaren's 2026 Formula 1 season has been characterised by a recovery effort that never quite came to fruition. Yet, team principal Andrea Stella insists the reasons for this are well understood, so he can be optimistic about 2027: "We are in a completely different place compared to the start of the season," he told Motorsport.com.

Whenever it seemed to have caught its rivals, McLaren found itself falling behind once again. A difficult start, followed by progress that culminated in a period of the championship when the MCL40 appeared capable of setting the technical benchmark, then a gradual decline in competitiveness and a return to the front at the Brazilian Grand Prix. This trajectory is not easy to interpret.

bullets: Racing Bulls confirmed Liam Lawson, 24, for the 2027 Formula 1 season last week, ahead of junior driver Nikola Tsolov, who is competing for the Formula 2 title. Lawson has scored 89 of the team's 114 points this year, helping Racing Bulls to a record fifth place in the constructors' championship. He has taken 15 points finishes from 20 grands prix, including a current streak of five top-nine results.

Team principal Alan Permane credited the improvement to Lawson trusting the team, sharpening his race craft and toning down his aggression, and called his turn one, lap one performances immense. Lawson's form held through a three-race stand-in spell at Red Bull for the injured Isack Hadjar, which Permane said he would have preferred to avoid. Permane said Racing Bulls could keep Lawson without abandoning its mandate of training young drivers.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
Liam Lawson's improved form made him too good for Racing Bulls to ignore for the 2027 Formula 1 campaign. But, as always, there's more than just a single factor behind that upturn in performances.

It was only last week that the 24-year-old was finally confirmed as staying with Red Bull's satellite team for next season, fending off a challenge by junior driver Nikola Tsolov who is currently vying for the Formula 2 crown.

Formula 1 & Motorsport.title: The Antonelli you don't know: Daily life with F1's newest champion
Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: The Antonelli you don't know: Daily life with F1's newest champion Autosport
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
There is one thing that physiotherapist Sergi Avila took a little while to understand. When Kimi Antonelli finally found himself with a free weekend, after weeks being spent between circuits, airports and training, the most logical choice would have been to stay at home: sleep a few extra hours, meet friends and switch off. Antonelli, instead, got in the car and went to a race track - perhaps to watch karting or MotoGP.

At first his performance coach inevitably tried to dissuade him, but then he understood that he was making a mistake as for Antonelli, simply going to a track does not mean working, but returning to the place where he feels happiest.

bullets: The 2027 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix will run from Friday 10 to Sunday 12 December 2027 at Yas Marina Circuit on Yas Island, later than the usual first weekend of December. F1's published dates confirm Abu Dhabi will close the 2027 season, and the weekend will include the capital's first F1 Sprint Race alongside the Grand Prix.

Fans can now register their interest in tickets through the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, which gives priority access when sales open and possibly an early bird deal. Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Oscar Piastri set for grid penalty at F1 Las Vegas GP Motorsport.com
bullets: McLaren's Oscar Piastri will take a 10-place grid penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix after exceeding his engine allowance. He had already used four internal combustion engines and needs a fifth Mercedes V6 to finish the 2026 season, following a reliability issue. McLaren said he has a good chance of recovering positions with overtaking in Saturday's race.

McLaren will also fit Mercedes' upgraded turbocharger, developed under the FIA's ADUO catch-up mechanism, with an expected performance benefit it describes as relatively small. Mercedes will trial the part on newly crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli's car. George Russell stays on the original specification to avoid a grid drop, as he has already reached his engine limit, according to Toto Wolff.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
McLaren driver Oscar Piastri is set for a 10-place grid drop at F1's Las Vegas GP for exceeding his engine allowance for the season. Piastri was already on the limit of four internal combustion engines for the year, but will need a fifth Mercedes V6 engine to finish the 2026 season.

As it is the first time he is exceeding his ICE allowance, the Australian will be docked 10 places on Las Vegas' starting grid. "Oscar will take a new Internal Combustion Engine in Las Vegas after a reliability issue," the team said in its event preview. "As it is his fifth of the season, he will take a 10-place grid penalty, but he has a good chance to recover positions with overtaking in Saturday's race."

bullets: Mercedes secured the 2026 constructors' championship at the São Paulo Grand Prix, one week after Kimi Antonelli won the drivers' title. Team principal and CEO Toto Wolff told BILD his celebration was subdued: he does not drink alcohol during the season, but had a vodka shot on the flight home with George Russell and Lewis Hamilton.

Wolff said he did not stay in São Paulo for a party because he is also a CEO and cannot afford a holiday, even for a night. He pointed to the more than 1,500 employees at Brackley and Brixworth behind the team's success. He said Mercedes wants to win both championships again next year.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth. Mercedes officially completed its return to the top of Formula 1 at the chaotic 2026 São Paulo Grand Prix, successfully locking down the constructors' world championship one week after Kimi Antonelli secured the drivers' title. But for team principal and CEO Toto Wolff, the historic milestone was not met with an explosive nightclub celebration in Brazil.

In a recent interview with the German publication BILD, Wolff revealed exactly how subdued his championship celebrations actually were. When asked if he had a go-to celebratory drink like Michael Schumacher's famous Bacardi and Cola, Wolff said he usually avoids alcohol entirely.

bullets: Liam Lawson will stay at Racing Bulls for the 2027 Formula 1 season, after a drawn-out process in which the team weighed him against Red Bull prospect Nikola Tsolov, aged 19. Lawson scored 75 points this season, helping the team towards a likely fifth place in the constructors' championship, its best result.

Team boss Alan Permane said keeping Lawson fits the team's development mandate, arguing a benchmark driver helps young talent develop. He called Lawson "immense" and said Arvid Lindblad will benefit from sharing data with him. Tsolov will wait at least another year for a race seat and will be reserve driver for both Red Bull teams in 2027. Permane has signed a five-year extension through 2031.

After concluding his journalism studies Filip decided to jump in at the deep end and become a freelance motorsports writer, which took him on a nomadic 50-country journey from Indianapolis to Le Mans and from Melbourne's Albert Park to the Dakar in Argentina. Born and raised in Belgium and now settled in sunny Barcelona, Spain, Filip first joined Motorsport.com in 2015 to help establish the Dutch edition before transitioning to the English-language team. In 2023 he became one of Motorsport Network's main F1 correspondents, with the 2026 season his fourth year on the ground at the majority of grands prix. Being Flemish, when he's not covering F1, he can likely be found watching the cycling instead, and he also has a soft spot for Southampton FC and the Toronto Blue Jays. Don't ask!

Formula 1 & Motorsport.summary: Wolff praises Antonelli despite ‘botched’ Japan start Formula 1
bullets: Kimi Antonelli won the Japanese Grand Prix at Suzuka, his second consecutive victory after his maiden win in China two weeks earlier. He started on pole ahead of Mercedes team mate George Russell but dropped to sixth at the start. He re-emerged in first place after pitting under the Safety Car, which followed Ollie Bearman's crash, and finished more than 13 seconds ahead of Oscar Piastri. Russell was fourth, and Antonelli became the youngest-ever leader of the Drivers' Championship.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff called Antonelli's launch "botched" and said the team need to improve their starts generally. He said Antonelli was very fast when it mattered, and that extending his stint by a lap made the difference to Russell's race. Wolff said Russell had struggled after a set-up change before Saturday's Qualifying. He also noted that Antonelli joined the Mercedes Junior Programme in 2018 and is now 19.

The extra race joins the Reverse Grid Race and Feature Race and restores the calendar to 14 races, after the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix was confirmed as no longer taking place in April.

The grid for the Opening Race will be set by each driver's second-fastest qualifying time rather than the fastest. It awards full points, counting towards both championships, with one point for fastest lap and none for pole. Managing Director Susie Wolff said the format maximises competitive track time, and the series said it was developed with the Canadian and Austin promoters.

bullets: Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' standings by 123 points from George Russell after 18 rounds of the 2026 season, with Lewis Hamilton 124 points behind in third. Antonelli will very likely clinch the title at the Mexico City Grand Prix if he finishes ninth or higher. The title could reach Abu Dhabi only if Antonelli scores no more points and Russell or Hamilton win every remaining race.

Co-branded Etihad and McLaren loungewear is being rolled out to premium cabins on long-haul flights until after the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in December. Etihad has decided rules are for budget carriers and instead painted an entire Boeing 787 Dreamliner in McLaren colours, making it the first time a Formula 1 team has ever appeared on a wide-body aircraft. Not since Pepsi talked Air France into painting a Concorde blue back in 1996 has a paint job looked this quick.

bullets: Istanbul Park will return to the F1 calendar next year under a new five-year contract, with the circuit layout, including the well-known Turn 8, remaining unchanged. Turkish Automobile Federation (TOSFED) president Eren Uclertopragi said the event will be overhauled, with more covered grandstands, fan zones, improved hospitality and better traffic flow and crowd management.

TOSFED is now both the national motorsport federation and the promoter, after the circuit was previously run by a private company. Uclertopragi said that company's priorities were not the sport, the fans or Formula 1. The paddock is being expanded, with capacity doubled and infrastructure rebuilt from scratch. The asphalt, which drivers described as like "driving on ice" in 2020, also needs to be in better condition. He credited FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem with helping secure the return.
Formula 1 & Motorsport.copy:

That applies to the technical regulations: striking a balance between satisfying drivers and purists on the one hand, and delivering the spectacle F1 wants to offer younger fans on the other, with a constant stream of overtaking moves for, let’s say, the TikTok generation.

Cycling.summary: Isaac Del Toro owes a lot to Pogačar, but wants to beat him IDLprocycling.com
bullets: Isaac del Toro, who turned 23 on Friday, will begin his fourth season with UAE Emirates-XRG in 2027. On the Cracks Podcast, the Mexican said he wants to be number one one day but accepts that for now this is Tadej Pogačar. Del Toro is second in the team's rankings, behind only Pogačar, and said he chose UAE after winning the 2023 Tour de l'Avenir because Pogačar rode there.

Del Toro finished third in the Tour de France standings with Pogačar's help, despite an illness that made him consider withdrawing, and Pogačar let him win Stage 2. He lost the 2025 Giro d'Italia to Simon Yates because of a tactical error. For 2027 he wants to raise his level, become more professional and follow his instincts more often in important races, rather than sticking rigidly to the plan.

Isaac del Toro turned 23 on Friday. The Mexican rider from UAE Emirates-XRG will begin his fourth season with the team in 2027, and he has clear plans for that time. Del Toro knows that UAE will have to do some balancing in 2027. Del Toro’s comments about the 2025 Giro d’Italia and his views on cycling’s history of doping have already been discussed.

Cycling.title: Tadej Pogačar advised by Paul Kimmage to speak to UAE boss about cycling’s past after five-time Tour de France winner claimed “doping doesn’t exist now”
Cycling.summary: Tadej Pogačar advised by Paul Kimmage to speak to UAE boss about cycling’s past after five-time Tour de France winner claimed “doping doesn’t exist now” Road.cc
bullets: Tadej Pogačar told La Gazzetta dello Sport that doping "doesn't exist now for the majority of the peloton" and is "not worth it", given the health risks and the professional consequences of being caught. Irish journalist and former professional Paul Kimmage questioned the claim in an interview with the road.cc Podcast. He suggested Pogačar ask his team principal, Mauro Gianetti, about cycling's past.

Gianetti, 62, rode professionally in the 1990s and has always denied personal involvement in doping. He told L'Équipe this year that he never used EPO, and said he was a "victim" of his riders' doping when he managed Saunier Duval, where Riccardo Ricco, Leonardo Piepoli and Juan José Cobo were caught up in scandals. Ricco, who now works in the ice cream business, suggested on Instagram that Pogačar's "selling ice cream" remark referred to him.
Cycling.copy:
Tadej Pogačar may be used to generating headlines on the bike, but it’s his recent remarks about doping – and, he claims, its lack of prevalence within the modern peloton – which have dominated cycling’s off-season discourse in recent days.

Speaking to La Gazzetta dello Sport, the five-time Tour de France winner claimed that doping “doesn’t exist now for the majority of the peloton” and that it simply is “not worth it”, due to both the health risks associated with performance enhancing drugs and the financial and professional implications of being caught.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Paul Kimmage questions Pogačar's claim] that doping "doesn't exist now" for most of the peloton, pointing to team principal Mauro Gianetti.
Cycling.angle: The debate involves UAE Team Emirates' leading rider and its principal, so it may draw reputational questions for a property ADNOC backs through XRG.

Cycling.title: Winning isn’t everything: Inside cycling’s high-stakes race for UCI points
Cycling.summary: Winning isn’t everything: Inside cycling’s high-stakes race for UCI points Cyclingnews
bullets: Data scientists are increasingly helping cycling teams maximise UCI points, which decide WorldTour status. The system runs in three-year cycles with 18 men's licences, and points earned to the end of 2028 will determine the 2029-2031 line-up. Only points from a team's top 20 scoring riders count, and relegation costs automatic race invitations, TV exposure and sponsor value.

XDS Astana, 21st in the 2024 rankings, hired data scientist Morgan Saussine, prioritised top-10 finishes over individual wins, signed 14 riders and finished fourth in 2025, while Cofidis were relegated. Researcher Louis Van Gaelen's model raised one team's points per rider from 375.3 to 824.7 in testing. Team Picnic PostNL has a 12-month licence for 2026, with the UCI expected to confirm 2027 registrations on 8 December.
Cycling.copy:
"After my presentation in Barcelona, teams wanted to chat and compare their models with mine. This is a growing field, whether it's in search of points or simply improving performance as a whole." That's Louis Van Gaelen. The Belgian's undertaking a PhD in health and artificial intelligence at the University of Antwerp. As a side project, the keen cyclist dug deep into professional cycling and, as his presentation at this year's Science & Cycling Conference revealed, 'roster optimisation for maximal UCI points'. It's not the sexiest of titles, but Van Gaelen's hobby, aligned with the work of an increasing number of data scientists around the sport, is proving critical for not only a team's success but their survival. It's time to talk about the merits of not aiming for victory…

The current UCI promotion and relegation system, rolled out in 2020, works in three-year cycles with 18 licences available to the men's WorldTour. The Women's WorldTour has 15 licences; however, demand for these spots is less competitive due to the limited number of teams willing to make the step up.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Teams use data to chase UCI points] as WorldTour status for 2029-2031 depends on results to the end of 2028.
Cycling.angle: Points strategy is reshaping how WorldTour teams race and recruit, which is relevant context for UAE Team Emirates XRG's competitors.

Cycling.title: Visma steps down as title sponsor of Visma-Lease a Bike team
Cycling.summary: Visma steps down as title sponsor of Visma-Lease a Bike team Cyclingnews
bullets: Visma will no longer be part of the Visma-Lease a Bike team name in 2027, the team confirmed on Thursday, but will remain as a "Founding Partner" of both the men's and women's teams. Visma has sponsored the team since 2019, a period in which it won 10 men's Grand Tours, including all three in 2023, and the 2025 Tour de France Femmes.

No replacement co-title sponsor has been named, and the team has been registered under its holding company name, Yellow B, in the initial application for 2027 UCI WorldTour and Women's WorldTour licences. Visma chief executive Merete Hverven said the company's strategic priorities have evolved, with several of its national brands set to appear on the 2027 jersey. Those sponsors will be revealed later.
Cycling.copy:
Visma-Lease a Bike have confirmed that Visma will no longer be part of the team name in 2027, with the Norwegian software company stepping down from its title sponsorship role but not leaving the team completely.

Such a move has been on the cards for months, and it was first reported back in February that Visma was looking to reduce the level of its investment, but the exact nature of the relationship from 2027 was made official on Thursday.
