Cycling.title: Pogacar signed his first contract for 60,000 euros a year: "If you win the Tour of the Future now, you sign for 300,000"
Cycling.summary: Pogacar signed his first contract for 60,000 euros a year: "If you win the Tour of the Future now, you sign for 300,000" Brujulabike.com
bullets: Tadej Pogačar's first professional contract with UAE Emirates, signed in summer 2018, paid 60,000 euros a year plus a 20,000 euro bonus for winning that year's Tour de l'Avenir, which he did. His agent Alex Carera told WielerFlits that first contracts then typically ran between 70,000 and 90,000 euros annually.

Carera said winning the Tour de l'Avenir now brings a 300,000 euro contract, citing Red Bull-BORA-hansgrohe's Lorenzo Finn. Teams now identify riders younger, with Carera running 16 scouts, and neo-professional contracts average more than three seasons, up from two a decade ago. Pogačar and Remco Evenepoel showed in 2019 that exceptional riders could win in the WorldTour from their debut.
Cycling.copy:
The emergence of Tadej Pogačar in professional cycling has not only changed the way of competing but also the price that teams are willing to pay for the future stars of this sport. His representative, Alex Carera, has revealed how much the Slovenian earned in his first contract with UAE Emirates, a figure that is very far from what the best under-23 talents can currently earn.

In the summer of 2018, Tadej Pogačar signed the contract that would take him to debut in the WorldTour the following season. At that time, UAE Emirates had managed to secure one of the most promising riders on the international scene for an amount that today would be hard to imagine.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Pogačar's first UAE Emirates contract paid €60,000] a year, against about €300,000 for a Tour de l'Avenir winner today.
Cycling.angle: Rising talent costs affect how UAE Team Emirates XRG and its academy compete for young riders.

Cycling.title: Cycling wants to put an end to last-minute controversial neutralizations in the Giro, Tour, and Vuelta
Cycling.summary: Cycling wants to put an end to last-minute controversial neutralizations in the Giro, Tour, and Vuelta Brujulabike.com
bullets: The Professional Cyclists' Association (CPA) wants grand tour organisers to define final-stage timing rules before each race from 2027. Its president, Adam Hansen, confirmed a meeting on 2 December with the UCI and the organisers of the Giro, Tour and Vuelta, and said the UCI shares the discomfort over last-minute changes.

The trigger was the 2026 Vuelta's final stage in Granada, where overall times were neutralised 9.8km from the finish, leaving Enric Mas the virtual winner. Hansen said the concern was equal conditions, as the narrow Alhambra climb stopped team cars passing to give mechanical help. Similar timing changes were made on the Tour's Montmartre circuit in 2025 and 2026. No agreement or new regulation has yet been approved.
Cycling.copy:
The Professional Cyclists' Association (CPA) wants to put an end to last-minute decisions that are altering the outcomes of the grand tours. Its president, Adam Hansen, has confirmed a meeting with the UCI and the organizers of the Giro, Tour, and Vuelta to establish clear rules before each race. The controversial neutralization of the final stage of La Vuelta 2026 in Granada has been one of the triggers.

The neutralizations of the final stages have become a recurring source of controversy in the grand tours. In recent years, both the Tour de France and La Vuelta a España have modified the way they account for the overall classification times when the race was practically finished. A situation that the Professional Cyclists' Association (CPA) wants to avoid starting in 2027.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [CPA seeks fixed final-stage rules] for the Giro, Tour and Vuelta from 2027, with a UCI meeting on 2 December.
Cycling.angle: Governance changes to grand tour finales could affect how UAE Team Emirates XRG plans for overall classification contests.

Cycling.summary: Big money, big plans, zero votes: The rise and fall of One Cycling Escape Collective
bullets: Escape Collective has reported that none of cycling's stakeholders voted in favour of One Cycling at a key Professional Cycling Council meeting in June 2025. That included the teams, represented by the AIGCP, and the riders, represented by the CPA. The UCI rejected the project that month and threatened to revoke WorldTour licences of teams and organisers that persisted.

The project was backed by €250m from Saudi Arabia's Surj group, a Public Investment Fund subsidiary, with 11 teams verbally committed as shareholders and nine more deliberating. It had applied for UCI licences for three new 2026 races, one in downtown New York City. Earlier this month, 26 teams became shareholders in Collective Cycling Group, One Cycling's successor, whose plans are not materially different.
Cycling.copy:
One Cycling was supposed to be the team-led reform effort that finally, after two decades of attempts, changed cycling forever. It promised changes to the sport’s economic model, its calendar, and how spectators watched racing.

Big money was behind it, in the form of €250M from Saudi Arabia’s Surj group, a subsidiary of the kingdom’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), with 11 teams verbally committed to becoming shareholders. Another nine were deliberating.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [No stakeholder voted for One Cycling] at the June 2025 UCI council, though its successor now has 26 team shareholders.
Cycling.angle: Reform of cycling's calendar and economics could affect the commercial landscape around UAE Team Emirates XRG and the UAE Tour.

Cycling.title: The UCI's registration rules strike again, delaying Shirin van Anrooij's debut with Canyon-SRAM
Cycling.summary: The UCI's registration rules strike again, delaying Shirin van Anrooij's debut with Canyon-SRAM Cyclingnews
bullets: Canyon-SRAM have announced that Dutch rider Shirin van Anrooij will race cyclo-cross in non-team kit from 27 November to 1 January. UCI rules mean her registration with the team cannot take effect until 1 January. She joined from Lidl-Trek on 1 November, two months ahead of schedule, but the move missed the UCI's mid-season transfer window of 1–15 August.

Van Anrooij is due to race alongside new teammate Zoe Backstedt at the UCI World Cup round in Ostrava on Friday and in about a dozen more races. The run ends with the UCI Cyclo-cross World Championships at the end of January. UCI Director of Sport Peter Van den Abeele said last year the federation was working with the riders' union, the CPA, to move the registration date to 1 November. That change has yet to be implemented.
Cycling.copy:
Shirin van Anrooij had big plans to start the cyclo-cross season with Canyon-SRAM after coming to a rare agreement to make the transfer from Lidl-Trek two months ahead of schedule.

Now, the Dutch rider will have to don a plain jersey for the first five weeks of her off-road season, Canyon-SRAM announced on Instagram. "Since joining Canyon-SRAM on Nov. 1, @shirnivananrooij has settled nicely into the team & familiarised herself with new equipment. In accordance with UCI regulations, she'll be registered independently & compete in non-team kit for cyclo-cross races from Nov. 27 until Jan. 1," the team wrote.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [UCI registration rules delay Van Anrooij's Canyon-SRAM debut], forcing her to race cyclo-cross in plain kit until 1 January.
Cycling.angle: Limited direct relevance to ADNOC, but UCI registration reform would affect when UAE Team Emirates XRG can show new signings in team kit.

Cycling.title: Tadej Pogačar weighs in on doping, big time
Cycling.summary: Tadej Pogačar weighs in on doping, big time Canadian Cycling Magazine
Cycling.copy:
It’s the off-season, but riders are still doing lots of interviews at training camps, junkets or events. And on Tuesday, arguably, if not the, greatest of all-time male cyclists Tadej Pogačar was talking about performance-enhancing drugs in the pro peloton. And he was pretty damn open on his thoughts.

Basically, he’s not too worried about it. In fact, the superstar even said he is pretty darn convinced most of his fellow riders wouldn’t go anywhere near any sort of boomba. He opened up to Italian newspaper La Gazzetta dello Sport. The five-time Tour de France winner, Giro d’Italia winner, Monument galore champ and two-time world champ offered a confident assessment of cycling’s current relationship with PEDs.

Cycling.title: Mads Pedersen calls out UCI over contract rules: 'It would be so easy to change'
Cycling.summary: Mads Pedersen calls out UCI over contract rules: 'It would be so easy to change' IDLprocycling.com
bullets: Mads Pedersen has criticised the UCI over a rule requiring World Team rider contracts to expire on 31 December of their final year, calling it "ridiculous". Article 2.15.119 of the UCI road regulations means riders who have joined new teams must train over the winter in their former team's jerseys and with un-branded equipment.

Speaking on the Lang Distance podcast, Pedersen suggested adding a clause letting riders use their new team's equipment from 1 December or the first team training camp. He said riders risk problems with former teams, including unpaid December salary, if seen using a new team's branded kit. The UCI previously said it would look into changing the rules, but nothing has been announced.
Cycling.copy:
Mads Pedersen calls out UCI over transfer contract regulation: "It's ridiculous...so stupid." Transfer news makes up a large chunk of the cycling world at this time of year. We have already seen some high-profile names switch teams: Roglič, Niewiadoma, Ganna, the list goes on. However, there are some difficulties in the contracts which lead, in Mads Pedersen's opinion, to a ridiculous scenario in the winter months.

2026 has seen a number of large names swap teams. Perhaps the longest and most in-the-spotlight contract story was Primož Roglič's with NSN. The Slovenian finally settled for the Swiss team after weeks of rumours and indecision.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Pedersen criticises UCI contract rule] forcing riders to train in old-team kit until 31 December.
Cycling.angle: A UCI governance issue affecting winter branding for all WorldTour teams, including sponsor visibility for UAE Team Emirates XRG's incoming riders.

Cycling.title: Giro d'Italia wants to move a week closer to the Tour de France
Cycling.summary: Giro d'Italia wants to move a week closer to the Tour de France Cycling Weekly
bullets: Giro d'Italia organiser RCS has asked the UCI for a calendar slot a week later, according to RCS boss Paolo Bellino, who said the request has strong government support. The move would ensure Italy's Republic Day on 2 June always falls within the race and cut the gap between the Giro and the Tour de France from five weeks to four.

Bellino argued this would encourage more riders to attempt the Giro-Tour double, last achieved by Tadej Pogačar in 2024 after a 26-year gap since Marco Pantani in 1998. Coach Andy Turner of ATP Performance said a shorter gap might not help and could even encourage riders to skip the Giro. The shift remains a wish-list item; the 2027 Giro will run entirely in May, from Trieste on 8 May to Rome on 30 May.
Cycling.copy:
The idea that the Giro d'Italia and the Vuelta a España ought to swap places on the cycling calendar is not a new one. With the Spanish race often too hot and the Giro peloton frequently enduring cold, wet days, the two seem ripe for a changeover.

Now, the Giro organiser RCS is seeking a calendar move, but nothing as drastic as swapping with the Vuelta. Instead, the Giro has asked the UCI for a slot a week later in the calendar. As well as ensuring that the Italian national holiday 'Republic Day' on 2 June would always fall within the race – just as Bastille Day falls within the Tour de France – RCS boss Paolo Bellino told Italy's BiciSport it would encourage more riders to attempt the Giro-Tour double.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [RCS asks UCI] to move the Giro d'Italia a week later, shrinking the Giro-Tour gap to four weeks.
Cycling.angle: A calendar change could affect how Tadej Pogačar and UAE Team Emirates XRG plan their Grand Tour seasons.

Cycling.summary: After Pogačar & Ricco, Del Toro brings up Lance Armstrong IDLprocycling.com
bullets: Isaac del Toro, the 22-year-old Mexican rider at UAE Team Emirates XRG, has joined a doping debate started by his teammate Tadej Pogačar. On the Mexican podcast Cracks, he said he never saw Lance Armstrong race and that Armstrong's era caused great damage and set cycling back significantly. He said he cannot defend Armstrong's decisions, whatever his achievements.

Pogačar had spoken of "a much greater awareness" of the harm banned substances cause, saying "no one wants to risk their life". He also joked that rule-breakers could end up selling ice cream, a reference to Riccardo Ricco's current career. Ricco replied on social media with a photo of Pogačar selling ice cream. Del Toro said he wished Armstrong's seven Tour wins had been legitimate.
Cycling.copy:
Following Tadej Pogačar's comments on doping in today’s cycling peloton, Isaac del Toro has joined the debate. The 22-year-old Mexican is Pogacar’s teammate at UAE Emirates-XRG, and it turns out shares his views when it comes to banned substances. Del Toro added to Pogačar's comments recently, and gave Lance Armstrong one hell of a beating on the Cracks Podcast.

“Many people want to stay active in the cycling world after their careers end, as a team manager or coach… One mistake and you run the risk of ending up selling ice cream, or something like that,” he said, jokingly referring to Ricco’s current career.

Cycling.title: Isaac del Toro recalls the lesson Van Aert taught him at the 2025 Giro d'Italia: 'That felt like the starting gun'
Cycling.summary: Isaac del Toro recalls the lesson Van Aert taught him at the 2025 Giro d'Italia: 'That felt like the starting gun' IDLprocycling.com
bullets: Isaac del Toro of UAE Team Emirates XRG has described how the 2025 Giro d'Italia shaped his career, in an interview with Cracks Podcast. He started as a domestique for Juan Ayuso, took the pink jersey in Siena on Stage 9 after attacking Wout van Aert in his first attack as a professional, and won a stage while wearing it.

Del Toro said he lost the race on Stage 20 over the Colle delle Finestre to Sestrière, when he forgot Van Aert was ahead in the early breakaway and Simon Yates caught the Belgian to take the pink jersey and overall victory. Yates finished ahead of Del Toro and Richard Carapaz. He said he accepted the consequences, that the loss left him angry and frustrated, and that afterwards he never held back again.
Cycling.copy:
Isaac del Toro had an amazing 2026, and that’s largely thanks to Wout van Aert. You read that right; in 2025, the Belgian rider from Visma | Lease a Bike dashed all the Giro dreams of a then-21-year-old Mexican rider from UAE Emirates-XRG. In an ultra-long interview with Cracks Podcast, Del Toro recalls that 2025 Giro d'Italia, a crucial turning point in his career.

Del Toro came to the 2025 Giro d'Italia as a domestique for Juan Ayuso. “After breaking my femur (in 2022, ed.), I’ve had problems with my kneecap, which sometimes causes me knee pain. I went to the 2025 Giro d’Italia with team leader Juan Ayuso, and even though I hadn’t been able to train as I’d hoped, it went surprisingly well,” he recalls.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Del Toro recalls losing the 2025 Giro] on Stage 20 and says the defeat drove him to never hold back again.
Cycling.angle: Gives human-interest material on a UAE Team Emirates XRG rider that ADNOC content teams could draw on.

Cycling.title: There Are the Biggest Changes Coming to Pro Cycling in 2027
Cycling.summary: There Are the Biggest Changes Coming to Pro Cycling in 2027 Outside Magazine
bullets: Pro cycling's 2027 season brings new team names and backers, according to Velo. Quick-Step is ending after 24 years, with The Wolfpack becoming Soudal-Safety Jogger. Canyon-SRAM is partnering with Scalable Capital, and the team formerly known as TotalEnergies now has Xefi as title sponsor.

TotalEnergies has withdrawn from the men's peloton to commit to a long-term deal with TotalEnergies-FDJ United, making it one of the biggest backers in the Women's WorldTour for five years. It also ended its non-naming deal with Netcompany Ineos. Primoz Roglič and Richard Carapaz have joined NSN Cycling Team, Kasia Niewiadoma-Phinney has moved to Lidl-Trek and Paula Blasi to Movistar, while Bahrain-Victorious has swapped Bianchi for Factor.
Cycling.copy:
Big changes are coming to pro cycling in 2027, and we aren’t talking about Tadej Pogačar not wearing a rainbow jersey. Tour de France hopefuls are making daring transfers. Long-time backers are switching allegiances.

Races will be in different places, teams will have unwieldy new names, and the UCI will have implemented more rules when competition restarts in January. A lot has changed in the world of pro cycling in the past few months – some things more important than others.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [TotalEnergies leaves the men's peloton] for a five-year deal with TotalEnergies-FDJ United, as new team names arrive for 2027.
Cycling.angle: Shifts in team sponsorship, including TotalEnergies' move into women's cycling, are a benchmark for UAE Team Emirates XRG's backers.

Cycling.title: Tadej Pogačar's return to Tour Down Under and Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Race will have to wait
Cycling.summary: Tadej Pogačar's return to Tour Down Under and Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Race will have to wait Cyclingnews
bullets: Tadej Pogačar will not return to the Santos Tour Down Under (19–24 January) or the Mapei Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Race (31 January), according to Daniel Benson's Substack. His team reportedly dropped the plan so it can closely monitor his recovery from a crash on stage 8 of the Vuelta a España, where he wore the red leader's jersey. Injuries included a concussion, a fractured left collarbone, a stable C7 cervical fracture and two further broken vertebrae.

Pogačar has raced both events only once, in 2019 as a first-year professional with UAE Team Emirates, finishing 13th overall in the Tour Down Under and 44th in the Great Ocean Road Race. Tour Down Under director Stuart O'Grady had said he was doing everything possible to attract him. In October, Pogačar said there was a "big chance" he would ride the Classics, the UAE Tour and the Tour de France in 2027, but that he still needed time to decide.
Cycling.copy:
January could have seen superstar Tadej Pogačar returning to Australia's Tour Down Under and Cadel Evans Great Ocean Road Race, which were his very first races as a professional with UAE Team Emirates in 2019. However, according to Daniel Benson's Substack, his team nixed the plan in order to closely monitor Pogačar's recovery from his crash in the Vuelta a España.

Pogačar suffered an alarming and unexpected early end to his 2026 season, crashing on stage 8 of the Vuelta a España while in the red leader's jersey. Initial medical examinations revealed that Pogačar suffered a concussion, fractures to his left collarbone, a stable C7 cervical fracture plus cuts and bruises though it was later revealed that he also had broken two additional vertebrae.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Pogačar will skip the Tour Down Under] and Great Ocean Road Race in January while his team monitors his Vuelta crash recovery.
Cycling.angle: Pogačar's recovery shapes UAE Team Emirates XRG's early 2027 plans, and he has said the UAE Tour is a 'big chance' for his return.

Cycling.title: MERIDA return to the WorldTour. Does the switch make sense for Soudal–Safety Jogger?
Cycling.summary: MERIDA return to the WorldTour. Does the switch make sense for Soudal–Safety Jogger? GRAN FONDO Cycling Magazine
Cycling.copy:
In 18 seasons on bikes bearing the big S, the team racked up 800 wins, took dozens of Monuments and broke the record for Tour stage wins. With Marcel Kittel on the Venge ViAS, they even helped bring disc brakes into the peloton. Standard kit today, they were hugely controversial at the time, with plenty of riders convinced they could cost someone their life. Now the Belgian outfit have a new name and a new bike sponsor. From 2027, Soudal–Safety Jogger will ride MERIDA bikes on an initial four-year deal, as will the AG Insurance–Soudal women’s team. It’s the REACTO for road stages and the TIME WARP for time trials. For the team, it’s the end of an era twice over. Specialized are leaving after nearly 20 years, and for the first time since the team was founded in 2003, Quick-Step are leaving too.

We’ll get used to the new bikes soon enough. As for getting the team name right every time, consider this our apology in advance. If the name REACTO still brings to mind Sonny Colbrelli lying in the Roubaix velodrome in 2021, caked in mud and crying tears of joy, you already have part of the answer. Pro racing has shaped MERIDA’s identity ever since they joined forces with Lampre in 2013. Their closest ties were with Bahrain, first as title sponsors alongside Vincenzo Nibali from 2017, then as bike suppliers until the end of 2025. Few riders gave those bikes better stories than Matej Mohorič. In 2022, he hit the dropper lever on his SCULTURA on the descent of the Poggio and rode to victory in Milan–San Remo. A year later, he rode the SILEX to its first gravel world title. After a season without a WorldTour team, MERIDA are back on the stage where those memories are made.

Eddy Merckx is still active in the cycling world. Speaking to Tuttobiciweb at a publicity padel tournament organised by his management agency, Pogačar left the door wide open for a Grand Tour clean sweep.

Cycling.title: Bizarre anti-doping outcome as banned Miguel Angel López inherits Tour of Austria victory from newly-banned Delio Fernández
Cycling.summary: Bizarre anti-doping outcome as banned Miguel Angel López inherits Tour of Austria victory from newly-banned Delio Fernández Cyclingnews
bullets: The International Testing Agency has banned Spanish former rider Delio Fernández for four years over a biological passport violation, so he cannot compete until 11 November 2030. The 40-year-old retired at the end of 2025. Independent experts unanimously concluded that changes in his values were highly likely caused by a prohibited substance or method, in samples collected in 2015 and 2023.

His results from 20 July 2015 to 9 August 2023 are wiped, so he loses the 2017 Tour of Austria title, which he inherited after Stefan Denifl was stripped over Operation Aderlass. The title passes to original third-placed Miguel Angel López, who is himself suspended. The ITA took over the case from the UCI in February 2026, and the Tribunal ruled on 12 November 2026. The decision can be appealed to CAS, and Fernández also faces a fine equal to his average gross annual cycling income.
Cycling.copy:
The International Testing Agency (ITA) has handed Spanish ex-racer Delio Fernández a four-year ban over a biological passport anti-doping rule violation. "In Delio Fernández Cruz’s case, independent experts unanimously concluded that the changes in his ABP values were highly likely to have been caused by a prohibited substance or method. The findings concerned samples collected during the Vuelta a Portugal on 28 July and 5 August 2015, and on 15 and 17 August 2023," the ITA statement read.

The ruling means that the 40-year-old, who retired at the end of 2025, is unable to compete until November 11, 2030. His results across two periods of his career have also been wiped – between July 20, 2015, the date of the first abnormal sample, and July 27, 2019, and between July 27, 2019 and August 9, 2023.

Cycling.title: Giro d'Italia organisers seek new calendar spot
Cycling.summary: Giro d'Italia organisers seek new calendar spot IDLprocycling.com
bullets: Giro d'Italia organiser RCS wants the race moved back by a week, and CEO Paolo Bellino said it has made this clear to the UCI with strong government support. The Giro currently starts in the first or second week of May. The change would place 2 June, Italy's Republic Day, regularly within the race.

Bellino gave two further reasons: likely better weather in the high mountains, and a shorter gap between the Giro and the Tour de France, matching the four weeks between the Tour and the Vuelta. He said this would let more riders attempt the Giro-Tour double. The article questions whether one less week of rest would help riders.
Cycling.copy:
The Giro d'Italia is always held in May, as the first Grand Tour of the year. In recent years, there have been calls to tweak the calendar, and the Giro’s organiser, RCS, now seems to want a different slot as well. And that could be bad news for riders who want to do the Giro-Tour double.

The Giro d'Italia always starts in the first or second week of May and ends in the final days of that spring month. Sometimes, very rarely, it extends into the first few days of June. It is precisely this latter scenario that RCS now hopes to make the norm by rescheduling the Giro d'Italia. “With strong support from the government, we have made it clear to the UCI that we want the Giro to take place a week later,” RCS CEO Paolo Bellino told BiciSport.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [RCS wants the Giro d'Italia moved] a week later, to include 2 June and shorten the gap before the Tour de France.
Cycling.angle: A shifted Grand Tour calendar could affect rider scheduling for UAE Team Emirates XRG.

Cycling.title: 'I hope it’s only the beginning' – Paul Seixas on his breakout year, dealing with pressure, and an eye-opening debut Tour de France
Cycling.summary: 'I hope it’s only the beginning' – Paul Seixas on his breakout year, dealing with pressure, and an eye-opening debut Tour de France Cycling Weekly
bullets: Paul Seixas, 20, became the youngest-ever winner of Il Lombardia, taking his first Monument with a solo attack 18.2km from the finish. The Decathlon CMA CGM rider extended his lead over Enric Mas to 48 seconds on the final climb. According to estimates based on Velon data, he climbed the 4km, 10% Civiglio at 7.1W/kg in a record 11:54.

Speaking to Cycling Weekly two days later, Seixas said he puts a lot of pressure on himself, but called it "good pressure". He had said he was "hugely disappointed" after finishing 15th in the road race at the World Championships in Montréal in September. France has had no male Tour de France winner since 1985, and Seixas is seen there as Bernard Hinault's heir apparent. He said he prefers to live his career day by day. Tadej Pogačar missed Lombardia while recovering from his Vuelta crash.
Cycling.copy:
I’m about halfway up the Mont Chauve climb out of Nice, my heart rate has been at 180bpm for half an hour already, and Paul Seixas is trying to talk to me about the area. Two days after his biggest triumph yet, becoming the youngest-ever winner of Il Lombardia, the 20-year-old finds himself cycling beside an out-of-breath English journalist.

“Nice houses!” I blurt, trying to make small talk while in oxygen deficit. “This is where all the rich people live,” Seixas replies, as untroubled by speaking his second language as he is by the gradient, before warning me about the descent – apparently the roads here can be very slippery. With that, the Decathlon CMA CGM rider tells our group he’s going to the front, and glides away. It isn’t so much an attack as a reminder that he is immeasurably better at riding a bike than any of us. I look down: we’re riding the same model of bike, the Van Rysel RCR-R Pro, but his appears to have jet engines attached.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Paul Seixas, 20, became the youngest Il Lombardia winner] with a solo attack 18.2km from the finish, beating Enric Mas by 48 seconds.
Cycling.angle: Seixas is already being compared with Pogačar, the leader of ADNOC-backed UAE Team Emirates XRG, who missed Lombardia while recovering from his Vuelta crash.

The UAE Tour is a major team objective and Isaac del Toro won it last winter, while Pogačar won it in 2021, 2022 and 2025. Strade Bianche was his season opener in 2024 and 2026, and he has won it four times. The Vuelta a Canarias has been cancelled and the AlUla Tour has reportedly followed.

Pogacar sustained a fractured collarbone, three vertebrae and a concussion at the Vuelta a España. Subsequently, he attempted to return to racing, and had also argued that he had begun his preparation for 2027 earlier.

bullets: The Tour du Rwanda will drop from eight stages to six in 2027, with two new UCI 1.1 one-day races added to attract more teams through extra UCI points. The 19th edition was presented on 20 November. The One Day Classic opens on 19 February, the six-stage Tour runs from 21 to 26 February, and the Kigalian Classic closes on 28 February. The stage race keeps its UCI 2.1 status.

The opening classic and the Tour's first stage overlap with the UAE Tour, which runs from 15 to 21 February. FERWACY put the total across the three races at 1,977 UCI points. The article notes that Saudi Arabia's AlUla Tour will not take place in January, and that the Tour of Qatar's return has been pushed back to 2028. FERWACY also announced the first women's Tour du Rwanda, listed for 29 September to 1 October 2027.
Cycling.copy:

The Rwanda Cycling Federation (FERWACY) presented the 19th edition on November 20 at the first Rwanda Cycling Day. The stage race keeps its UCI 2.1 status. The ‘One Day Classic’ opens the programme on February 19 with 111km from Gicumbi to Nyamata. The six-stage Tour runs from February 21 to 26, and the ‘Kigalian Classic’ closes the programme on February 28 with about 118km around Kigali.

Cycling.title: “Sooner or later, I’ll give it a try”: Pogačar sets his sights on riding all three Grand Tours in the same year
Cycling.summary: “Sooner or later, I’ll give it a try”: Pogačar sets his sights on riding all three Grand Tours in the same year Brujulabike.com
bullets: Tadej Pogačar has said he intends to try winning the Giro d'Italia, Tour de France and Vuelta a España in the same season, though not in 2027. Asked about Eddy Merckx's claim that he could do it, he told a padel event run by his agency, A&J Sport Management, "sooner or later I will try it", as reported by Tuttobiciweb. The challenge would cover 63 Grand Tour stages over about four months.

His 2027 priorities are a sixth Tour de France win, which would take him past the five shared by Anquetil, Merckx, Hinault and Induráin, plus Paris-Roubaix, the only Monument he has not won, and the Vuelta, where a fall while leading ended his 2026 race. The 2027 World Championships in Haute-Savoie are another target. UAE Team Emirates-XRG sports director Joxean Fernández Matxin has said he dreams of winning all three Grand Tours with different leaders.
Cycling.copy:
Tadej Pogacar continues to expand his goals and is now contemplating one of the greatest challenges in cycling history: competing in and winning all three Grand Tours in the same season. The Slovenian has stated that he wants to attempt it at some point in his career, although his priorities for 2027 include conquering his sixth Tour de France, winning Paris-Roubaix, and returning to the Vuelta a España.

Few things seem out of reach for Tadej Pogačar, but there are still records that even the greatest champions in history have not achieved. One of them is winning the Giro d'Italia, the Tour de France, and the Vuelta a España in the same season, a challenge that the UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider has already acknowledged he wants to face.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Pogačar says he will try all three Grand Tours] in one season "sooner or later", but not in 2027, when he targets a sixth Tour.
Cycling.angle: Pogačar's ambitions keep UAE Team Emirates XRG, which ADNOC backs, at the centre of cycling's biggest stories heading into 2027.

Cycling.title: Winning the Giro, Tour and Vuelta in 2027 is Demi Vollering’s plan, and she has already discussed it with her team
Cycling.summary: Winning the Giro, Tour and Vuelta in 2027 is Demi Vollering’s plan, and she has already discussed it with her team Brujulabike.com
bullets: Demi Vollering is considering trying to win the Giro d'Italia, Tour de France and Vuelta a España in the same season in 2027 and has already discussed the idea with her team, the newly renamed Total Energies FDJ United-SUEZ. The Vuelta moves from May to 3-10 October in 2027, which makes the plan possible. The Giro runs from 29 May to 6 June and the Tour from 30 July to 7 August.

Vollering told Dutch broadcaster NOS she does not yet want to make the triple an official objective, saying she must still be fresh enough. She won the Giro, a second Tour and the World Championship in 2026, and has already won all three Grand Tours across her career. Her team says defending the Tour title and the rainbow jersey are priorities for 2027. She is also preparing for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Annemiek van Vleuten first raised the idea of a triple.
Cycling.copy:
After a 2026 season in which she conquered the Giro d'Italia, the Tour de France, and the World Championship, Demi Vollering is already starting to think about an even greater challenge. The Dutch rider is considering the possibility of trying to win all three Grand Tours in the same season and acknowledges that she has already discussed this option with her team, the newly renamed Total Energies FDJ United-SUEZ.

The idea has gained momentum thanks to a significant modification of the women's calendar. In 2027, the Vuelta a España will no longer take place in May but will move to October, a decision that opens, for the first time in several years, a particularly favorable window to chain the Giro, Tour, and Vuelta without compromising the preparation for the French round.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Vollering weighs Giro, Tour and Vuelta triple] in 2027, after the Vuelta moves to 3-10 October, and has discussed it with her team.
Cycling.angle: The reshaped 2027 women's calendar affects the build-up to the Tour and the wider women's season that UAE Team Emirates XRG also races in.

Cycling.title: UCI upholds Schreiber’s disqualification, but Luxembourg refuses to move on
Cycling.summary: UCI upholds Schreiber’s disqualification, but Luxembourg refuses to move on Brujulabike.com
bullets: The UCI has upheld the disqualification of Marie Schreiber from the women's European Cyclocross Championship, held on 7 November in Zeddam, the Netherlands. Schreiber crossed the line first in a close sprint against Lucinda Brand but was relegated to second for a deviation in her trajectory. Brand is the champion, and Ceylin del Carmen Alvarado is third. The UCI told the Luxembourg federation (FSCL) on 19 November that the commissioners acted correctly.

FSCL president Marcel Gilles said the response was too general and the board will decide its next steps. Technical director Christian Helmig said the UCI treats the incident as a racing incident, which cannot be appealed under Article 12.4.001 of its disciplinary regulations. The Court of Arbitration for Sport is among the options being considered. Any step must take Schreiber's wishes into account.
Cycling.copy:
The controversy over the outcome of the 2026 European Cyclocross Championship remains unresolved. The International Cycling Union (UCI) has supported the decision of the commissioners who relegated Marie Schreiber to second place after crossing the finish line ahead of Lucinda Brand. However, the Luxembourg Cycling Federation (FSCL) finds the response insufficient and is considering new actions to defend its rider.

Almost two weeks after the controversial sprint that decided the women's European cyclocross championship, held on November 7 in Zeddam (Netherlands), the UCI has communicated its position to the Luxembourg federation.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [UCI upholds Schreiber's disqualification] from the European Cyclocross Championship, while Luxembourg weighs further action.
Cycling.angle: A UCI governance dispute with no direct link to ADNOC or UAE Team Emirates XRG, but it shows how officiating is being challenged.

Cycling.title: From rookie to challenging Pogacar in 7 months - British time trialist reveals himself at La Vuelta
Cycling.summary: From rookie to challenging Pogacar in 7 months - British time trialist reveals himself at La Vuelta CyclingUpToDate.com
bullets: Callum Thornley, a 23-year-old Scot riding his first Grand Tour, finished fourth in the opening 9.4-kilometre individual time trial of the 2026 Vuelta a España in Monaco. He was five seconds behind winner Tadej Pogacar and four seconds ahead of Wout van Aert. He later came within two seconds of a stage victory in Jerez de la Frontera.

Thornley, from Peebles in the Scottish Borders, joined Red Bull–BORA–hansgrohe's senior roster in January 2026 after a season in the team's under-23 Rookies programme. He was the first Rookies rider promoted to the WorldTour team. He also finished inside the top ten at both the World and European Time Trial Championships, and won the British under-23 time trial title in 2025.
Cycling.copy:
When the 2026 Vuelta a España rolled down the start ramp in Monaco for its opening 9.4-kilometre individual time trial, almost every pre-race headline belonged to Tadej Pogacar and Wout van Aert. By the time the dust settled along the Principality's Formula 1 corners, however, a 23-year-old Scottish neophyte riding his first Grand Tour had forced his way into the conversation. Finishing fourth on the stage, just five seconds behind winner Pogacar and four seconds clear of Van Aert, Callum Thornley announced himself to the wider cycling public in the sharpest possible terms.

Standing 1.90 metres tall and weighing 76 kilograms, Thornley possesses the classic physiological blueprint of a modern rouleur and time trial specialist. Yet his rise to the front end of a WorldTour Grand Tour leaderboard was anything but conventional. Hailing from Peebles in the Scottish Borders, far removed from the traditional heartlands of European road racing, Thornley entered 2026 as a first-year professional on Red Bull–BORA–hansgrohe's senior roster, having spent the previous season in the team's under-23 development ranks.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Callum Thornley finished fourth] in the Vuelta's opening Monaco time trial, five seconds behind Tadej Pogacar.
Cycling.angle: Pogacar won the Vuelta's opening time trial, and a young time-trial rival is emerging. The article does not mention ADNOC or UAE Team Emirates XRG.

Cycling.title: Tadej Pogačar opens up about the mental toll of his crash
Cycling.summary: Tadej Pogačar opens up about the mental toll of his crash KarloBag.eu
bullets: Tadej Pogačar has told Belgian broadcaster Sporza that the first three weeks after his Vuelta a España crash were painful and that he was not feeling mentally well. He said he did not recognise himself and needed a break from competitive pressure. He also told Gazzetta dello Sport that his mood deteriorated sharply a few days after the crash, though he did not describe it as a medical diagnosis.

The crash came at the end of August on stage eight of the Vuelta, while he wore the red jersey. UAE Team Emirates-XRG confirmed a concussion, a displaced left collarbone fracture and a C7 fracture, and a later CT scan in Slovenia found T1 and T2 fractures too. The injuries ruled him out of the World Championships and European Championships, ending a season that included a fifth Tour de France title.
Cycling.copy:
Slovenian cyclist Tadej Pogačar has spoken about the period following his serious crash at the Vuelta a España, revealing that the consequences were not only physical. In an interview with Belgian broadcaster Sporza, he said that the first three weeks were painful and that he was not feeling mentally well. He admitted that at one point he did not recognize himself and that, alongside physical rehabilitation, he also needed a break from the constant pressure of competition. His account illustrates how a serious injury can change the everyday life of an athlete accustomed to training sessions, races and a strictly planned schedule. Although his condition gradually improved, the mental aspect of recovery remained an important part of his experience following the accident.

In his interview with Sporza, Pogačar described the first three weeks after the crash as an especially difficult period. He did not feel like his usual self and did not want to attribute everything solely to his injuries. According to his explanation, his mood may have been affected by a combination of the accident and everything that had accumulated during a demanding season. He pointed out that athletes also go through periods when they feel unwell and that his body probably needed a break. He also stressed that mental well-being is extremely important and that sometimes the mind needs rest just as much as the body.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Pogačar describes mental toll] of his Vuelta crash, which left three fractured vertebrae and ended his 2026 season.
Cycling.angle: Pogačar is the headline rider of UAE Team Emirates XRG, so his recovery and return affect the team's profile and ADNOC's cycling programme.

Cycling.title: AlUla Tour removed from the calendar due to war in Iran
Cycling.summary: AlUla Tour removed from the calendar due to war in Iran IDLprocycling.com
bullets: AlUla, the Saudi Arabian city, has withdrawn from cycling with immediate effect, ending both the AlUla Tour race and its jersey sponsorship of the WorldTour team Jayco-AlUla, which began in 2023. Escape Collective reported the news on Saturday. The team, owned by Gerry Ryan, must now find a new jersey sponsor for 2027. The article links the exit to security risks and air-travel disruption following the war involving the United States, Israel and Iran, which began in late February 2026.

The article says Formula 1 cancelled its Saudi Arabia and Bahrain Grands Prix earlier this year, and the UCI cancelled the Urban Cycling World Championships in Riyadh in October. GreenEDGE Cycling had faced funding and ownership restructuring, delaying its 2027 WorldTour licence application. The men's and women's teams are not seen as immediately at risk, and new investors have been attracted. The team will race next season under a new name and identity, with a greater focus on young talent and a tighter budget. Other Middle East projects may also be in jeopardy.
Cycling.copy:
AlUla has withdrawn from cycling effective immediately, Escape Collective reported on Saturday morning. The city in Saudi Arabia organised a cycling race earlier this year called the AlUla Tour, as well as being the jersey sponsor of the WorldTour team Jayco-AlUla since 2023. Both partnerships have now been terminated.

Fernández retired in April 2025 and the Spaniard is now 40 years old. His ban came into force on November 12, 2026, and will run through to November 11, 2030. Cycling.copy:
The UCI is set to make an overhaul of the Lugano charter for 2027. That could be good news for bike design, given it sets the design regulations compliant bikes must adhere to. But I wish I didn’t have to think about what might come next.

In my column last week, I said the UCI should stay out of gravel, while defending the expansion of wheel sizes. That got me thinking – when I’m testing a bike intended for the road, and potentially racing, I always look for the UCI sticker on the frame. Why? I’m not sure. Cycling.summary: Ex-UCI president slates “nonsense” pro cycling reform plans: “Insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting different results” Road.cc
bullets: The Collective Cycling Group launched on Wednesday with 24 teams from the men's and women's pelotons, aiming to overhaul the calendar and economic model of professional cycling. Thirteen men's WorldTour teams, 11 Women's WorldTour teams and two ProTeams signed shareholder agreements in Brussels, holding 95 per cent of the company. Five seed investors hold the rest, having put in €25 million.

Former UCI president Brian Cookson told road.cc the plan is not fundamentally different from reform proposals and breakaway leagues that have failed over 20 years. UAE Team Emirates-XRG, Jayco AlUla and Groupama-FDJ United have no intention of signing up, and Tour de France organisers ASO remain opposed. The UCI is due to set out its own reform outline in Benidorm on 9 December.
Cycling.copy:
Professional cycling’s longstanding obsession with reform has been given another makeover this week, thanks to the advent of the Collective Cycling Group, the latest coalition of teams and ambitious billionaires seeking to overhaul the sport’s calendar and economic model.

The merits and aims of the new group, however, have been questioned by former UCI president Brian Cookson, who believes there is nothing “fundamentally different” between this latest initiative and the litany of reform proposals and breakaway leagues that have emerged, and failed, over the past 20 years.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [24 teams launch Collective Cycling Group] to reform the calendar and finances; UAE Team Emirates-XRG will not join.
Cycling.angle: UAE Team Emirates XRG staying outside the group matters for ADNOC; the UCI's 9 December reform outline is the next point to monitor.

Cycling.title: Pope Leo XIV names Merckx, Indurain, Seixas, Vollering and up to 100 cyclists at the Vatican
Cycling.summary: Pope Leo XIV names Merckx, Indurain, Seixas, Vollering and up to 100 cyclists at the Vatican Brujulabike.com
bullets: Pope Leo XIV will receive about 100 representatives of cycling at the Vatican on the morning of Monday 23 November, the UCI has announced. The audience is organised with the Dicastery for Culture and Education of the Holy See and covers the main cycling disciplines, including para-cycling.

Guests include Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, Miguel Induráin, Greg LeMond, Chris Froome, Vincenzo Nibali and Mark Cavendish, alongside current riders Demi Vollering and 20-year-old Paul Seixas, plus federation and race organiser representatives. UCI president David Lappartient said it is an opportunity to reinforce cycling's commitment to peace and intercultural dialogue. The UCI plans to symbolically hand over bicycles for young people in vulnerable situations assisted by Caritas of Rome.
Cycling.copy:
The Vatican will host an unusual meeting for professional cycling next Monday, November 23. Pope Leo XIV will receive a hundred representatives of this sport, including legends like Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault, and Miguel Induráin, along with current champions like Demi Vollering and Paul Seixas. An audience that also recalls the previous visits of Peter Sagan and Egan Bernal to Pope Francis, both with very special bicycles as protagonists.

The International Cycling Union (UCI) has officially announced that the meeting will take place on the morning of Monday, November 23, in the Vatican. The initiative is organized together with the Dicastery for Culture and Education of the Holy See and will feature a representation from the main cycling disciplines, including para-cycling.

Cycling.summary: The new bike for Roglič, Carapaz and Girmay: CUBE signs with NSN Cycling Team Brujulabike.com
bullets: CUBE will return to the UCI WorldTour in 2027 as the bicycle supplier to NSN Cycling Team, replacing SCOTT. It will supply both the WorldTeam and the development team, using the Litening C:68X AERO and AIR road bikes and the Aerium C:68X TT time-trial bike. The announcement came a day after NSN confirmed the signing of Primož Roglič for 2027.

The roster will also include Richard Carapaz, Santiago Buitrago, Lennert Van Eetvelt, Kasper Asgreen and Biniam Girmay. Girmay won three stages and the green jersey at the 2024 Tour de France on CUBE bikes. General director Kjell Carlström said NSN will focus more on general classification in 2027. CUBE has also launched a Litening AERO C:68X SLX Team Edition, available from March 2027.
Cycling.copy:
CUBE has officially announced its return to the UCI WorldTour in 2027 after reaching an agreement with the NSN Cycling Team. The German brand will become the new bicycle supplier for the Spanish-Swiss structure, replacing SCOTT and accompanying a team that is making some of the most significant moves in the transfer market.

The announcement comes just a day after the surprising signing of Primož Roglič by NSN for 2027 was confirmed. The four-time Vuelta winner will join a roster that will also include Richard Carapaz, Santiago Buitrago, Lennert Van Eetvelt, Kasper Asgreen, and Biniam Girmay.

Cycling.title: ‘Who is influencing whom and why?’ – Some of cycling’s biggest backers are spinning a sponsorship spiderweb, but what are the risks?
Cycling.summary: ‘Who is influencing whom and why?’ – Some of cycling’s biggest backers are spinning a sponsorship spiderweb, but what are the risks? Cyclingnews
Cycling.copy:
At Spain’s biggest cycling races next year, one sponsor will be ubiquitous: Lidl. Plastered across the red leader’s jersey at the men’s and women’s Vuelta a España will be the logo of the German supermarket chain; it’ll also adorn barriers and finish gantries at the Volta a Catalunya and the Itzulia Basque Country; and in each and every race, riders from Lidl-Trek, also emblazoned with the discount chain’s red-yellow-blue coat of arms, will be competing. Given the team’s big-spending habits of recent times, it’s not unfeasible that a Lidl rider will win (many) a Lidl race.

The newly announced sponsorship deals – which are in addition to the Lidl Deutschland Tour, and come three years after Lidl was a major sponsor of the 2023 UCI Road World Championships – are another sign of Lidl’s commitment and interest in mass-participation sport; alongside cycling, it has also significantly invested in football and handball. As the company's customer base and profits reach new heights, so too does its marketing strategy. To promote an active lifestyle to its millions of loyal and new customers, it wants to be seen as the supermarket of choice for athletes and active people.

bullets: Tadej Pogacar has completed his off-season and is returning to full training after several months of recovery from injuries and a busy year. He ended his season at the Vuelta a España, where a crash left him with a concussion and a fractured collarbone and vertebra. He could not return in time for the European Championships in Slovenia, and he learned of two further fractured vertebrae.

Pogacar wrote on Instagram that it was now time to get serious, after attending friend Eddie Dunbar's wedding in Ireland with Urska Zigart. He will take part in a UAE Team Emirates - XRG training camp in December, and the team's media day is on 18 December, a day after Team Visma | Lease a Bike. Richard Carapaz said Pogacar remains a cut above the other Tour contenders.

Cycling.title: Tour de Romandie saved as Primeo Energie steps in as sponsor for both women’s and men’s races
Cycling.summary: Tour de Romandie saved as Primeo Energie steps in as sponsor for both women’s and men’s races Cyclingnews
bullets: Primeo Energie has become main sponsor of the Tour de Romandie's women's and men's races for the next two editions, rescuing the women's event, which was postponed in 2026 owing to a lack of funds. The Swiss electricity company has sponsored the mountains classification jerseys since 2022. The three-day women's race returns in 2027, starting on 10 September.

Organisers had sought to close a 10 per cent budget shortfall before the 2026 race, in which Tadej Pogačar won four of five stages and the overall classification. The 80th men's edition begins with a prologue on Tuesday 27 April and features loop-style stages, each almost entirely within one canton, which organiser Richard Chassot said let the public see riders repeatedly and eases rising safety demands. Primeo Energie CEO Cédric Christmann said backing the women's race was important to him.
Cycling.copy:
After a lack of funds was cited as a major contributing factor in the cancellation of the 2026 Tour de Romandie Féminin, the race will return in 2027 with Primeo Energie stepping up to sponsor both women’s and men’s races.

The Swiss electricity company have sponsored the races’ mountains classification jerseys since 2022, the first year of the women’s race, but will now be the main sponsor of both events for the next two editions.

Cycling.line: [Primeo Energie becomes Tour de Romandie sponsor] for both women's and men's races, reviving the women's event in 2027.

Cycling.title: The Giro d’Italia is on board with the new cycling Super League: “We would be willing to reach an agreement”
Cycling.summary: The Giro d’Italia is on board with the new cycling Super League: “We would be willing to reach an agreement” Brujulabike.com
bullets: The Giro d'Italia has said it is willing to work with Collective Cycling Group (CCG), the project backed by 24 professional teams and successor to ONE Cycling. Luca Guercilena, the new Giro director and former Lidl-Trek manager, told Domestique he believed RCS Sport would be willing to reach an agreement. This came 24 hours after the teams announced CCG. He said professional cycling needs a different business model, and that any deal must respect the UCI's authority and regulations.

RCS Sport has not signed any agreement with CCG. Guercilena said the Tour de France is a reference point, but the Giro wants its own identity. In December, he and RCS Sport officials will visit team training camps to discuss expenses, logistics and race participation. He also wants riders such as Paul Seixas, Isaac del Toro and Giulio Pellizzari to prioritise the 2027 Giro. He prefers improving conditions to paying large participation bonuses. The article notes that Tour de France organiser ASO has historically opposed projects that could threaten its position.
Cycling.copy:
The new cycling Super League has just been presented and has already found a potential ally among the major organizers. The Giro d'Italia has opened the door to collaborate with Collective Cycling Group, the project driven by 24 professional teams to transform the cycling business. Its new director, Luca Guercilena, believes that the sport needs a different economic model and is willing to explore agreements with the new organization.

Just 24 hours after 24 teams officially announced the creation of Collective Cycling Group, RCS Sport has expressed its interest in collaborating with this initiative, the successor to the ONE Cycling project.

Cycling.title: Benidorm brings cycling’s biggest stars together for a UCI Gala that could shape the future of the WorldTour
Cycling.summary: Benidorm brings cycling’s biggest stars together for a UCI Gala that could shape the future of the WorldTour Brujulabike.com
bullets: The UCI will hold its first UCI Cycling Gala at the Cultural Centre of Benidorm on Wednesday 9 December, starting at 7:45pm. The ceremony will recognise the best riders, teams and countries from the 2026 UCI road rankings and present the new UCI Fan Awards. Categories include Achievement of the Year, Sprinter of the Year, Climber of the Year, Rising Star of the Year and Domestique of the Year, each with ten nominees, five men and five women. It will be broadcast on television in Europe and on the UCI YouTube channel elsewhere.

The UCI WorldTour and Women's WorldTour Seminar will run in Benidorm on 9 and 10 December. The UCI has confirmed it will present the general lines of its professional cycling reform there, developed with Deloitte as strategic adviser after the Future of Road Cycling consultation. Topics include calendar reorganisation, a more balanced distribution of income, joint exploitation of commercial and audiovisual rights, team finances and rider safety, with the first measures possible from 2029. The seminar follows the 18 November launch of Collective Cycling Group, a commercial Super League initially made up of 24 teams.
Cycling.copy:
Benidorm is just 20 days away from becoming the center of international cycling. On December 9, the Alicante city will bring together some of the great figures of the peloton at the first UCI Cycling Gala. A ceremony that will serve to reward the best of 2026, but that will coincide with a particularly important moment for the future of professional cycling: the UCI will present there the first lines of the WorldTour reform, just a few days after the birth of a new Super League driven by 24 teams.

The Cultural Center of Benidorm will host, on Wednesday, December 9, starting at 7:45 PM, the first edition of a gala that aims to become an annual event on the cycling calendar.

Cycling.line: [UCI holds its first Cycling Gala in Benidorm on 9 December] and will present WorldTour reform outlines the same week.

Cycling.title: 24 teams come together to form Collective Cycling Group, the latest venture aiming to 'unlock the value' of pro cycling
Cycling.summary: 24 teams come together to form Collective Cycling Group, the latest venture aiming to 'unlock the value' of pro cycling Cyclingnews
bullets: Twenty-four men's and women's WorldTour and ProTeam squads have signed up to the Collective Cycling Group (CCG), announced on Wednesday to "develop and market selected commercial rights and activities" and strengthen the sport's economic model. The UK-registered company is essentially the same entity as the failed One Cycling project, renamed on 2 June 2026, with Oliver Ciesla replacing Richard Plugge as director.

According to Escape Collective, 13 of 18 men's WorldTour teams have joined, with UAE Team Emirates-XRG among the five absentees. In the women's WorldTour, 10 of 14 teams are reportedly signed up, with UAE Team l'IMAD among those declining. The UCI rejected One Cycling last June as incompatible with its governance framework, and its response to the CCG may become clearer after the WorldTour seminar on 9-10 December 2026.
Cycling.copy:
Following the collapse of the One Cycling project that aimed to reform professional cycling into a more lucrative business model, a new group has officially made its presence known with similar aims but stronger support. The Collective Cycling Group (CCG) issued a press release on Wednesday announcing the new movement.

It was stated that 24 teams from the men’s and women’s WorldTour and ProTeam ranks have already signed up, and that there are ongoing discussions with additional teams. Several teams have shared news of the announcement, indicating that they are part of the movement, but not all have.

bullets: Primož Roglič has signed a one-year contract with NSN Cycling Team for 2027, ending months of speculation about his future after his time with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe. The 37-year-old five-time Grand Tour winner joins Richard Carapaz and Lennert Van Eetvelt as new signings for the Swiss WorldTour team's general classification ambitions.

Roglič arrives with 93 career victories, the most among active men's riders apart from Tadej Pogačar. He finished second at the most recent Vuelta a España, eighth at last year's Tour de France, and is the reigning European time trial champion. NSN general manager Kjell Carlström said Roglič still has passion and drive, while Roglič linked the move to the team's "Never Say Never" name.
Cycling.copy:
After months of speculation, Primož Roglič will continue his career into 2027, having signed with NSN Cycling Team on a one-year contract. The 37-year-old looked to be heading for retirement after his time with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe came to an end – despite being the reigning European time trial champion and having finished second at the Vuelta a España in September – but with NSN, he has found a place for the final chapter of his storied career.

A five-time Grand Tour winner, Roglič will make up part of the Swiss WorldTour team’s general classification ambitions, alongside fellow new signings for 2027, Richard Carapaz and Lennert Van Eetvelt.

That factor is Tadej Pogacar's likely absence from the start line in May as the UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider outlined his intention to chase history at the Tour de France. With the dominant force in cycling potentially out of the picture, organisers RCS Sport hope the rest will come knocking.

Cycling.title: Gran Premio NYC confirmed as fifth UCI men's race in US next year with sponsor search active to add women's event
Cycling.summary: Gran Premio NYC confirmed as fifth UCI men's race in US next year with sponsor search active to add women's event Cyclingnews
bullets: The Gran Premio New York City will return as a UCI 1.2-ranked one-day race on Sunday 16 May 2027, for its fourth edition. It is the fifth UCI men's road event in the US next year, and Battenkill's 1.2 race on 22 May in Cambridge, New York makes a doubleheader possible, with the two venues less than 200 miles apart.

The professional race starts about 10 minutes ahead of roughly 3,000 amateurs in the Gran Fondo New York, sharing an 85-mile (137km) course along the Hudson River through Bergen County, New Jersey and Rockland County, New York. GFNY CEO Uli Fluhme said the pro race is only feasible because of the amateur event's road closures, and that a stand-alone pro race would cost about $1m. Organisers are seeking sponsors for a women's race, which they estimate would add $100,000. Team presentation is on 14-15 May at the NYC Bike Expo in Fort Lee.
Cycling.copy:
The Gran Premio New York City (GP NYC) returns as a UCI one-day race in 2027, as organisers confirmed that a fourth edition is now on the international calendar for Sunday, May 16.

The 1.2-ranked men's race expects to attract a more robust field of North American and international teams as it is no longer an isolated UCI race as Battenkill's 1.2 event on May 22 in Cambridge, New York makes the pair of road races appealing as a doubleheader, separated geographically by less than 200 miles.

bullets: Tadej Pogačar has ended his off-season and said it is "now time to get serious" as he prepares for 2027. The Slovenian ended his 2026 campaign early after crashing out of the Vuelta a España, and has since travelled, run and attended fellow rider Eddie Dunbar's wedding in Killarney, Ireland.

He will meet his UAE Team Emirates-XRG team for a training camp in south-east Spain next month, where his full 2027 programme is due to be confirmed in mid-December. He is set to return at the UAE Tour in February, a race he has won three times. His suggested main goals are the Tour de France, the Vuelta a España and the Road World Championships.
Cycling.copy:
Tadej Pogačar has announced that it's "now time to get serious" as he calls an end to his off-season ahead of ramping up preparations for a racing return in 2027. The Slovenian former world champion was forced to end his 2026 campaign prematurely after crashing out of the Vuelta a España. After recovering from his injuries, he has spent recent weeks travelling and enjoying time away from serious training and racing.

Pogačar's latest stop came in Ireland at the weekend, where he and his partner Urška Žigart attended sometime training partner Eddie Dunbar's wedding in Killarney. He wasn't riding his road bike while in Ireland, but was spotted by several locals riding a mountain bike and going for a run in the woods.

Cycling.title: La Vuelta 2027 Route Reveal Set for January 14 as Super Worlds Reshape the Racing Calendar
Cycling.summary: La Vuelta 2027 Route Reveal Set for January 14 as Super Worlds Reshape the Racing Calendar TodoMountainBike
bullets: Organisers Unipublic will unveil the full route of the 82nd Vuelta a España on Thursday 14 January 2027 at 8:00pm local time, at the Fuxan os Ventos Municipal Auditorium in Lugo, Spain. The race runs from 4 to 26 September 2027, starting in Santiago de Compostela and finishing in Madrid. It returns to a Spanish Grand Départ after starts in Lisbon in 2024, Turin in 2025 and Monaco in 2026.

The race is moved later by the 2027 UCI Cycling World Championships, which run from 24 August to 5 September in Haute-Savoie, France. The Vuelta starts one day before they end, so riders targeting both events face a demanding transition, especially those who also ride the Tour de France. At least four Galician stages are planned, but stage profiles and most host locations are yet to be announced.
Cycling.copy:
The 2027 Vuelta a España will follow an unusual schedule, with all three weeks of racing taking place in September and the opening stages returning to Spain. Organizers have confirmed when the complete route for the 82nd edition will be unveiled, setting the stage for a Grand Tour that will be directly affected by the 2027 UCI Cycling World Championships in France. The revised calendar could force some of the sport's biggest names to rethink their late-season racing plans.

Unipublic, the company behind the Spanish Grand Tour, has announced that the official route presentation will take place on Thursday, January 14, 2027, at 8:00 p.m. local time, at the Fuxan os Ventos Municipal Auditorium in Lugo, northwestern Spain. The event will reveal the start and finish locations of all 21 stages, along with the distribution of mountain stages, time trials, and other major challenges awaiting the peloton.

Rapha is making a return to the WorldTour peloton as the official performance partner to the Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe team. The British company has been absent from the top-level peloton this season after its deal to supply the EF Education men's and women's teams expired at the end of the 2025 season.

Rapha and Red Bull have entered into a "multi-year agreement", with the company replacing Specialized as the team's kit manufacturer. In announcing the deal, Rapha hailed Red Bull's willingness to disrupt the sports it enters, including cycling, "bringing an unsurpassed level of global engagement, scale and energy".

bullets: Paul Seixas, 20, says winning the Tour de France is a dream he cannot yet achieve, and that the World Championships road race may be his main goal for 2027. He finished fourth on his Tour debut this year as its youngest starter in 89 years. He spoke in Japan after winning the Saitama Tour de France criterium ahead of Brandon McNulty.

He said the Worlds matter to him because of his family ties, and that he may have only one chance to ride them there. He also wants to ride a Grand Tour but has not chosen which, with race planning normally done around December. He expects to open 2027 with Strade Bianche and then Tirreno, and contract talks for 2028 onwards follow his return home.
Cycling.copy:
There's no question that at just 20 years of age, Paul Seixas looks one of the most likely contenders to inherit the position which Tadej Pogačar currently occupies as cycling's number one rider. But even with his warranted confidence as the youngest Monument winner since 1944, the French star can admit that winning the Tour de France remains a dream out of reach for the moment.

Fourth on debut and the youngest starter for 89 years at the Tour de France this year, Seixas delivered on his promise to finish one place down on the podium, behind Pogačar, Remco Evenepoel, and the other most likely heir to the Slovenian's crown, his UAE teammate Isaac del Toro, who is just 23.

Cycling.title: Tadej Pogačar came last in his first ever race, and Colnago's new film shows why he didn't care
Cycling.summary: Tadej Pogačar came last in his first ever race, and Colnago's new film shows why he didn't care IDLprocycling.com
bullets: Tadej Pogačar finished last in his first race, according to POG1: The Making of a Legend, a Colnago Cultura documentary that premiered on Friday 13 November. Directed by Filippo Barcatta, it is free on Colnago's YouTube channel in English, Italian and Slovenian. Pogačar, a five-time Tour de France winner, says he did not mind the result and had a very fun time, despite racing older and bigger riders.

The film focuses on his childhood in Komenda and his motivation rather than data. Andrej Hauptman, his mentor and now a sports director at UAE Team Emirates-XRG, recalls first seeing him at a children's race in Ljubljana, where he was the smallest rider. Pogačar says his motivation now comes from his teammates, whom he calls a second family, and he talks about a quieter life after racing. The release comes as he recovers from the crash that ended his Vuelta a España and kept him out of the road World Championships and Il Lombardia.
Cycling.copy:
Tadej Pogačar has won the Tour de France five times, but his racing career started at the very back of the field. In POG1: The Making of a Legend, a new Colnago Cultura documentary, the Slovenian looks back at his childhood in Komenda and at a debut that gave no hint of what was coming. He wasn't bothered by the result. In fact, he says he loved it.

The film, directed by Filippo Barcatta, premiered on Friday 13 November and is free to watch on Colnago's YouTube channel. We've been spoiled with Pogačar documentaries recently, following Anatomy of a G.O.A.T, which covered the physiology side of the Slovenian phenom.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [Colnago documentary POG1 looks back] at Pogačar finishing last in his first race, released 13 November on YouTube.
Cycling.angle: Content about the star of UAE Team Emirates XRG keeps his profile high during recovery; the team's sports director features in the film.

Cycling.title: Inside the numbers as elite Tour de France cyclists prepare for 2027 Grand Départ
Cycling.summary: Inside the numbers as elite Tour de France cyclists prepare for 2027 Grand Départ Times & Star
bullets: Carlisle will host the finish of Stage One of the 2027 Tour de France Grand Départ on Friday 2 July 2027, with Stage Two starting in Keswick on Saturday 3 July. Stage One covers 185km with 2,000m of elevation, while Stage Two runs 223km to Liverpool with 2,800m of elevation. An estimated 422,000 spectators are expected at the start and finish areas, and visitors are forecast to bring £48m in additional spending to Cumbria.

The Joy Makers volunteering programme has attracted more than 25,000 registrations for about 9,000 places, and more than 300 people aged 18 to 25 will join a Readiness to Work programme. Cumbria Combined Authority chief executive John Barradell said the event lets the county present itself as a place to invest. Live UK coverage will be on Channel 5 and TNT Sports, and nearly 150 million people watched live coverage of the 2026 Tour.
Cycling.copy:
ELITE cyclists are heading to Cumbria in July 2027 for the world famous Tour de France Grand Départ, a major sporting event which is set to be a significant logistical challenge for authorities as well as a catalyst for economic development.

Carlisle will host the finish to Stage One of the Grand Départ on Friday July 2, 2027 and the beginning of Stage Two, in Keswick, on Saturday July 3, 2027. Cyclists embark on a Grand Départ, or great departure, each year before heading to France for the world famous race series.

Cycling.title: Chinese Bike Giant XDS Threatens Bombshell Split from Astana WorldTour Team
Cycling.summary: Chinese Bike Giant XDS Threatens Bombshell Split from Astana WorldTour Team Outside Magazine
bullets: Chinese bike maker XDS is reportedly threatening to end its contract with the XDS-Astana WorldTeam ahead of the 2027 season, two years into a five-year deal, according to L'Equipe. The paper says XDS is exploring joining another top-ranked team, and that a decision could come as soon as this week.

XDS took co-title sponsorship of the team at the start of 2025 and put its X-Lab bikes into the Tour de France. L'Equipe reports the company is anxious about Yana Seel's return to a commercial role at Astana in October, citing past tensions with general manager Alexander Vinokourov, though Seel said she returned to work with him. Pardus has meanwhile partnered with Xefi, the team formerly known as TotalEnergies, through 2029.
Cycling.copy:
The marriage between Chinese bike giant XDS and the XDS-Astana WorldTeam might be on the brink of divorce. According to reports from L’Equipe, XDS is threatening to terminate its contract with Alexander Vinokourov’s team ahead of the 2027 season. That’s just two years into a five-year deal.

Any possible split would be devastating for the team. XDS helped save Team Astana from WorldTour relegation when it brought big budget and its wildly popular X-Lab bikes to the squad at the start of 2025.
Cycling.label: CYCLING
Cycling.line: [XDS threatens to leave Astana] two years into a five-year deal, L'Equipe reports, with a decision possibly this week.

Cycling.title: No room for Pogačar Tour de France win in UCI Awards, Gillespie makes it
Cycling.summary: No room for Pogačar Tour de France win in UCI Awards, Gillespie makes it Sticky Bottle
bullets: The UCI's 2026 Fan Vote Awards shortlists give Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) just one nomination, for 'feat of the year' after winning Milan-Sanremo. His record-equalling fifth Tour de France win, with five stage victories, is not listed, and he is absent from the 'climber of the year' category. Lara Gillespie (UAE Team L'IMAD), the Irish road race champion, is one of 10 riders nominated for 'sprinter of the year'.

The awards have five categories: feat, domestic, young rider, climber and sprinter of the year. Each category mixes men and women, and the five winners are chosen by fan vote. They will be presented at the UCI annual gala in Benidorm on 9 December. UCI president David Lappartient said riders write the season's story, but it resonates most with fans, and the Fans' Choice Awards will show which moments meant the most to the public.
Cycling.copy:
Tadej Pogačar (UAE Team Emirates-XRG) may have won a record-equalling fifth Tour de France, claiming five stage wins along the way, but there is no place for his Tour performance in the achievements of year selected by the UCI.

While the Slovenian does get one nomination in the UCI's annual awards, while others get three, it is for winning Milan-Sanremo. His Tour ride does not even merit a nomination for 'climber of the year' and is instead completely overlooked.

Cycling.summary: Reports suggest XDS may withdraw sponsorship of the XDS-Astana team before the scheduled 2029 date Cyclingnews
Cycling.copy:
Reports in the French sports paper L'Equipe have emerged questioning the future of bike manufacturer XDS as a name sponsor of the XDS-Astana team. Escaping what was, at one stage, almost certain relegation from the WorldTour at the end of 2025, the Kazakh squad have been one of the revelations of the men’s peloton in the last two years since the Chinese bike manufacturer came on board.

In 2025, XDS’s first year as a title sponsor, the team cleverly targeted UCI points at races all over the World, closing the year as the fourth-ranked team and escaping the drop to ProTeam level. While they slipped to sixth place in 2026, they still finished ahead of the vast bulk of WorldTour teams, with Netcompany-Ineos and Soudal-QuickStep among the outfits trailing in their wake.

UAE Pro League & GCC Football.title: Al-Qadsiah break Al-Fayha resistance late to go top of Saudi Pro League
UAE Pro League & GCC Football.summary: Al-Qadsiah break Al-Fayha resistance late to go top of Saudi Pro League Arab News
bullets: Al-Qadsiah beat Al-Fayha 2-0 on Matchday 13 to go top of the Saudi Pro League, one point ahead of Al-Hilal, who have two games in hand. Turki Al-Ammar scored in the 71st minute after coming on as a substitute, and Mohammed Abu Al-Shamat added a second in the 89th. The match was played at Al-Ettifaq Stadium because Al-Qadsiah's usual home was unavailable due to winter overseeding.

Al-Qadsiah were without injured players Mateo Retegui and Christopher Bonsu Baah and had thrashed Shabab Al-Ahli 5-1 in the AFC Champions League Elite on Tuesday. Al-Fayha, coached by Fabio Carille, defended in a 5-3-2 block, and goalkeeper Orlando Mosquera made three saves. Brendan Rodgers said the team had to work very hard and praised Al-Ammar's impact. Carille said he was proud of his side. Al-Qadsiah's new Aramco Stadium has yet to be officially inaugurated for league games.
UAE Pro League & GCC Football.copy:
ALKHOBAR: It is a rare sight when Brendan Rodgers’ Al-Qadsiah go 70 minutes without scoring in the Saudi Pro League. The Knights of the Eastern Province were tested by a stubborn Al-Fayha on their return to league action on Matchday 13, but ultimately secured the victory after a decisive substitution by Rodgers.

Al-Qadsiah’s usual home, Prince Mohammed bin Fahad Stadium, was unavailable due to winter overseeding, so the match was played at rivals’ Al-Ettifaq Stadium. Al-Qadsiah’s new and highly awaited Aramco Stadium has yet to be officially inaugurated for league games.

UAE Pro League & GCC Football.summary: Emaar Super Cup a ‘celebration of UAE football’ says Musab Al Marzooqi Gulf News
bullets: UAE Pro League CEO Musab Al Marzooqi has previewed Sunday's Emaar Super Cup final between Al Ain and Shabab Al Ahli at Mohammed bin Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi. Shabab Al Ahli are in their third consecutive final, while Al Ain, unbeaten in last season's league and President's Cup winners, sit a point ahead of them in the table. Shabab Al Ahli won both meetings this season, 2-0 in the league and 3-2 in the President's Cup Round of 16.

Two fan zones accompany the final. The Abu Dhabi Fan Zone outside the stadium runs from 26 to 29 November, 5pm to 10pm daily, with face painting, football challenges and a merchandise store, and the Dubai Creek Harbour Fan Zone opens on 27 November. Al Marzooqi said the aim is a good experience for all ticket holders and a chance to show Emirati football to international supporters.
UAE Pro League & GCC Football.copy:
Dubai: UAE Pro League CEO Musab Al Marzooqi believes Sunday's Emaar Super Cup between Al Ain and Shabab Al Ahli has all the ingredients for a memorable occasion, describing the showdown as a “celebration of football” in the Emirates.

Speaking exclusively to Gulf News, Al Marzooqi looked ahead to the eagerly anticipated final, which will see two of the country's most successful clubs go head-to-head at Mohammed bin Zayed Stadium in Abu Dhabi.
